primary_endpoint_description: Shift in the distribution of modified Rankin Scale scores at 90 days
brief_rationale: The primary outcome showed a statistically significant shift toward better 90-day modified Rankin Scale outcomes with endovascular therapy versus medical management alone (generalized odds ratio 1.37, 95% CI 1.11–1.69; P=0.004), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Two primary outcomes: composite maternal sepsis or death, and composite stillbirth or neonatal death or sepsis.
brief_rationale: Azithromycin significantly reduced the maternal composite (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.56–0.79; P<0.001), but not the newborn composite (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95–1.09; P=0.56). Because the co-primary outcomes were mixed and no overall success rule is stated, overall primary-endpoint success is unclear.

primary_endpoint_description: Survival with a favorable neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score 1 or 2) at 30 days
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 20% with extracorporeal CPR versus 16% with conventional CPR (odds ratio 1.4, 95% CI 0.5–3.5; P=0.52), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: All-cause mortality before discharge home by day 90
brief_rationale: The trial hypothesized lower mortality with the restrictive strategy, but mortality was 14.0% versus 14.9% with the liberal strategy (difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.4 to 2.6; P=0.61), so the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary objectives comparing BA.1-adapted vaccines with 30-μg BNT162b2: superiority in BA.1 NT50 and noninferiority in BA.1 seroresponse.
brief_rationale: Both bivalent doses and the 60-μg monovalent vaccine met the superiority and noninferiority objectives, but results were mixed or incompletely stated across all BA.1-adapted dose groups, and no overall success rule for the multiple primary comparisons is provided.

primary_endpoint_description: Unfavorable status at 72 weeks after randomization, defined as a composite of death, treatment failure, treatment discontinuation, loss to follow-up, or tuberculosis recurrence.
brief_rationale: The prespecified noninferiority margin was 12 percentage points. The risk difference for BPaLM versus standard care was -9 percentage points (96.6% CI, -22 to 4) in the per-protocol analysis, with the upper confidence bound below the margin; the abstract concludes that BPaLM was noninferior.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall response to zanubrutinib versus ibrutinib
brief_rationale: Overall response is explicitly identified as the primary end point, and the abstract states that prespecified interim analyses showed zanubrutinib was superior to ibrutinib for this endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of necrotizing enterocolitis (Bell's stage IIa or higher), moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, or death at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 46.3% with expectant management versus 63.5% with early ibuprofen. The upper boundary of the one-sided 95% CI for the absolute risk difference was -7.4 percentage points, below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 10 percentage points (P<0.001 for noninferiority), so the primary endpoint met the success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Number of long glances away from the roadway and standard deviation of lane position during simulated drives after training
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary outcomes favored the intervention at 1 and 6 months: fewer long glances (incidence rate ratio 0.64; P<0.001) and lower lane-position variability (differences -0.21 and -0.22; P<0.001 for interaction).

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline at 18 months in the Clinical Dementia Rating–Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score.
brief_rationale: The adjusted mean CDR-SB increase was 1.21 with lecanemab versus 1.66 with placebo, a favorable difference of -0.45 (95% CI, -0.67 to -0.23; P<0.001), demonstrating statistically significant superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of a major adverse limb event (above-ankle amputation or major limb reintervention) or death from any cause.
brief_rationale: The primary composite favored surgery significantly in cohort 1 (HR 0.68, P<0.001) but not in cohort 2 (HR 0.79, P=0.12). Because these parallel-cohort trials had mixed primary-outcome results and no overall success rule is stated, a single publication-level determination is not defensible.

primary_endpoint_description: Survival to hospital discharge
brief_rationale: The primary outcome favored both active strategies over standard defibrillation: survival was 30.4% with DSED versus 13.3% with standard defibrillation (RR 2.21, 95% CI 1.33–3.67) and 21.7% with vector-change defibrillation versus 13.3% (RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.01–2.88). Both confidence intervals excluded the null in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death from any cause or hospital discharge with Cerebral Performance Category 3 or 4 within 90 days after randomization.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 32.3% of the 36-hour group and 33.6% of the 72-hour group (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.77–1.26; P=0.70), so longer fever prevention did not demonstrate superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Event-free survival, defined as time to disease progression, relapse, development of a second malignant neoplasm, or death.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored brentuximab vedotin: 3-year event-free survival was 92.1% versus 82.5%, with a hazard ratio for event or death of 0.41 (95% CI, 0.25–0.67; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to first Plasmodium falciparum infection detected by blood-smear examination over 24 weeks
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored both CIS43LS doses over placebo, with efficacy of 88.2% for 40 mg/kg and 75.0% for 10 mg/kg; both comparisons were statistically significant (P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Number of days alive and out of the hospital at 90 days after randomization
brief_rationale: The adjusted mean difference favored haloperidol by 2.9 days, but the 95% CI crossed zero (-1.2 to 7.0) and P=0.22; therefore, haloperidol did not achieve significantly greater days alive and out of hospital than placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: F-VASI75 response at week 24, defined as at least a 75% improvement from baseline in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored ruxolitinib cream in both trials: 29.8% versus 7.4% in TRuE-V1 and 30.9% versus 11.4% in TRuE-V2, with P<0.001 for each comparison, meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Risks of colorectal cancer and colorectal cancer–related death at 10 years
brief_rationale: The two explicitly identified primary endpoints had mixed results: colorectal cancer risk was significantly lower with screening invitation (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70–0.93), whereas colorectal cancer mortality was not significantly reduced (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.64–1.16). The abstract does not state the overall success rule for these multiple primary endpoints.

The abstract explicitly identifies the reported microvascular and cardiovascular outcomes as prespecified secondary outcomes. It does not explicitly identify or sufficiently report a prespecified primary endpoint for assessment.

primary_endpoint_description: Cumulative incidence of a quarterly measured glycated hemoglobin level of 7.0% or higher that was subsequently confirmed.
brief_rationale: The primary metabolic outcome differed significantly across the four treatment groups (global P<0.001), with lower event rates for glargine and liraglutide than for glimepiride and sitagliptin, demonstrating favorable superiority among treatments.

primary_endpoint_description: At least a 4-point decrease (improvement) in the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire score after 12 weeks without treatment failure.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 56.4% of the dual-bronchodilator group versus 59.0% of the placebo group (adjusted odds ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.60–1.37; P=0.65), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to worsening heart failure (unplanned hospitalization or urgent visit for heart failure) or cardiovascular death
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite outcome occurred less often with dapagliflozin than placebo (16.4% vs 19.5%; hazard ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.73–0.92; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Relapse, measured by future emergency department visits, surgeries, or growth of secondary stones.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored removal: time to relapse was significantly longer (log-rank P<0.001), with an 82% lower relapse risk (hazard ratio 0.18; 95% CI, 0.07–0.44). Thus, the favorable superiority criterion was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death or persistent organ dysfunction on day 28
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred more often with vitamin C than placebo (44.5% vs 38.5%; risk ratio 1.21, 95% CI 1.04–1.40; P=0.01), a statistically significant result in the unfavorable direction. Thus, vitamin C did not meet a favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was progression-free survival. RVD plus ASCT significantly prolonged progression-free survival versus RVD alone (median 67.5 vs 46.2 months; hazard ratio expressed for RVD alone vs transplantation, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.23–1.91; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrence-free survival at 2 years
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint was 2-year recurrence-free survival. ctDNA-guided management was noninferior to standard management (93.5% vs 92.4%; absolute difference 1.1 percentage points, 95% CI −4.1 to 6.2), with the lower confidence bound above the prespecified −8.5-percentage-point noninferiority margin.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to the first severe asthma exacerbation in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The higher-dose albuterol-budesonide combination significantly reduced the risk of the primary endpoint versus albuterol alone (hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.62–0.89; P=0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Hemoglobin response, defined as an increase from baseline of at least 1.5 g/dL sustained at two or more scheduled assessments at weeks 16, 20, and 24.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 16 of 40 patients (40%) receiving mitapivat versus 0 of 40 receiving placebo, with an adjusted difference of 39.3 percentage points (95% CI, 24.1 to 54.6; P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the Achilles' tendon Total Rupture Score at 12 months
brief_rationale: The primary outcome did not differ significantly among nonoperative treatment, open repair, and minimally invasive surgery (P=0.57), with pairwise comparisons providing no evidence of superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary end points of event-free survival and pathological complete response (0% viable tumor in resected lung and lymph nodes), assessed by blinded independent review
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary end points significantly favored nivolumab plus chemotherapy: event-free survival HR 0.63 (97.38% CI, 0.43–0.91; P=0.005) and pathological complete response 24.0% versus 2.2% (OR 13.94; 99% CI, 3.49–55.75; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of preeclampsia with severe features, medically indicated preterm birth before 35 weeks' gestation, placental abruption, or fetal or neonatal death.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite outcome occurred less often with active treatment than with control (30.2% vs 37.0%; adjusted risk ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.74–0.92; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Patient-reported success at 15 months, defined as feeling very much or much improved on the Patient Global Impression of Improvement questionnaire.
brief_rationale: The prespecified 10-percentage-point noninferiority margin was met: the adjusted risk difference for mini-slings versus midurethral slings was 4.6 percentage points (95% CI, -2.7 to 11.8), with P<0.001 for noninferiority.

primary_endpoint_description: SALT score of 20 or less at week 36
brief_rationale: In both phase 3 trials, significantly more patients achieved the primary outcome with either baricitinib dose than with placebo (P<0.001 for each dose versus placebo), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival as determined by blinded independent central review
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored trastuzumab deruxtecan, with a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.28 (95% CI, 0.22–0.37; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

The abstract explicitly identifies overall survival as a key secondary endpoint. Although progression-free survival is mentioned, it is not explicitly identified as the prespecified primary endpoint in the supplied information.

primary_endpoint_description: Absence at 3 years of a composite endpoint comprising functional, structural, and biologic abnormalities after thyroidectomy without versus with postoperative radioiodine
brief_rationale: The event-free rate was 95.6% without radioiodine and 95.9% with radioiodine, for a difference of -0.3 percentage points (two-sided 90% CI, -2.7 to 2.2). The abstract explicitly states that this met the prespecified noninferiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) over 3.5 years.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 2.1% of the CT group versus 3.0% of the invasive coronary angiography group (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.46–1.07; P=0.10), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized rate of severe asthma exacerbations
brief_rationale: The intervention significantly reduced the explicitly identified primary endpoint versus usual care (0.69 vs 0.82 exacerbations annually; hazard ratio 0.85, 95% CI 0.72 to 0.999; P=0.048), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Neurologic outcome at 3 months according to the Cerebral Performance Category scale, dichotomized as good versus poor outcome.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups: poor outcome occurred in 90% with antiseizure treatment versus 92% with standard care (difference, 2 percentage points; 95% CI, -7 to 11; P=0.68), so superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. Darolutamide plus androgen-deprivation therapy and docetaxel significantly reduced the risk of death versus placebo plus the same background therapy (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.57–0.80; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

The abstract reports a favorable, statistically significant reduction in COVID-19–related hospitalization or death through day 28, but it does not explicitly identify this or any other measure as the prespecified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints of pathological complete response at definitive surgery and event-free survival; this report presents the event-free survival analysis.
brief_rationale: Event-free survival was significantly longer with pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy (36-month EFS 84.5% vs 76.8%; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.48–0.82; P<0.001). The abstract also states that the other primary endpoint, pathological complete response, was significantly higher in an earlier analysis.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints: prevalence of PCR-confirmed active yaws in the entire trial population and prevalence of serologically confirmed latent yaws among asymptomatic children aged 1–15 years, both at 18 months.
brief_rationale: Both coprimary endpoints favored three rounds of mass azithromycin: active yaws was 0.04% versus 0.16% (adjusted RR for control vs experimental, 4.08; 95% CI, 1.90–8.76), and latent yaws was 3.28% versus 6.54% (adjusted RR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.12–3.70). Both confidence intervals excluded the null in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored relatlimab–nivolumab over nivolumab: median progression-free survival was 10.1 versus 4.6 months, with a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.75 (95% CI, 0.62–0.92; P=0.006), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of participants with virologic or clinical treatment failure by 96 weeks, estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method.
brief_rationale: Treatment failure by 96 weeks was lower with dolutegravir-based ART than with standard care (0.14 vs 0.22; difference, -0.08; 95% CI, -0.14 to -0.03; P=0.004). The favorable confidence interval supported superiority and therefore satisfied the noninferiority objective.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy endpoint: composite of Covid-19-related hospitalization or death from any cause by day 28.
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy endpoint occurred in 0.7% with remdesivir versus 5.3% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.13, 95% CI 0.03–0.59; P=0.008), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Number of adults treated for confirmed tuberculosis within 14 days after presenting to the health center for evaluation during the 16-month intervention period
brief_rationale: The intervention increased the explicitly identified primary outcome versus routine care (342 vs 220 patients; adjusted rate ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.21 to 2.01). The confidence interval excludes no effect and favors the intervention, meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: GPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 (no visible pustules) at the end of week 1
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 54% of patients receiving spesolimab versus 6% receiving placebo, a favorable difference of 49 percentage points (95% CI, 21 to 67; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of hospitalization or death through day 29
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored molnupiravir. Superiority was demonstrated at the planned interim analysis: hospitalization or death occurred in 7.3% with molnupiravir versus 14.1% with placebo (difference, -6.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -11.3 to -2.4; P=0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Effect of chemotherapy on invasive disease-free survival and whether that effect was influenced by the 21-gene recurrence score.
brief_rationale: The primary objective is explicit, but the abstract does not state its prespecified overall success criterion. It reports benefit in premenopausal women, no benefit in postmenopausal women, and no increasing benefit with recurrence score, without establishing how these findings determine overall primary-endpoint success.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to first occurrence of death from cardiovascular causes or incident heart failure (outpatient symptomatic heart failure or heart failure leading to hospitalization).
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 11.9% with sacubitril-valsartan versus 13.2% with ramipril (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.78–1.04; P=0.17), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Functional outcome on the modified Rankin scale at 90 days.
brief_rationale: For the primary endpoint, EVT alone had an adjusted common odds ratio of 0.84 (95% CI, 0.62 to 1.15; P=0.28) versus alteplase plus EVT. It met neither the superiority criterion nor the prespecified noninferiority margin of 0.8.

primary_endpoint_description: Occurrence within 1 year of a major adverse cardiac or cerebrovascular event, defined as death from any cause, myocardial infarction, stroke, or repeat revascularization.
brief_rationale: The prespecified noninferiority criterion required the upper bound of the 95% CI for the hazard ratio to be below 1.65. The observed hazard ratio was 1.5 (95% CI, 1.1–2.2), so the upper bound exceeded the margin; noninferiority was not demonstrated (P=0.35).

primary_endpoint_description: First occurrence of laboratory-confirmed type A or B influenza.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 7.8% of IIV4c recipients versus 16.2% of comparator recipients, corresponding to vaccine efficacy of 54.6% (95% CI, 45.7% to 62.1%); the confidence interval excluded no efficacy and favored IIV4c.

primary_endpoint_description: Least-squares mean change from baseline on the Aberrant Behavior Checklist modified Social Withdrawal subscale (ABC-mSW) over 24 weeks.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome showed no favorable superiority of oxytocin over placebo: the between-group least-squares mean difference was -0.2 (95% CI, -1.5 to 1.0; P=0.61).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death or inability to walk approximately 10 ft (3 m), independently or with a walker or cane, at 60 days after randomization
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 18.5% with spinal anesthesia and 18.0% with general anesthesia (relative risk 1.03, 95% CI 0.84–1.27; P=0.83). Spinal anesthesia did not demonstrate superiority, so the primary endpoint did not meet the success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage of patients with clinical remission, assessed using the three-component Mayo score, during the 10-week induction and maintenance periods through week 52.
brief_rationale: Clinical remission was significantly more frequent with ozanimod than placebo during both induction (18.4% vs 6.0%; P<0.001) and maintenance (37.0% vs 18.5%; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion in both periods.

primary_endpoint_description: Dual primary endpoints of progression-free survival and overall survival, tested sequentially in the PD-L1 combined positive score ≥1 population, the intention-to-treat population, and the PD-L1 combined positive score ≥10 population.
brief_rationale: Both primary endpoints favored pembrolizumab and were statistically significant in each sequentially tested population. Progression-free survival hazard ratios ranged from 0.58 to 0.65 (P<0.001), and overall survival hazard ratios ranged from 0.61 to 0.67 (P≤0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Blood culture-confirmed typhoid fever
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less often with Vi-TCV than with the MenA control vaccine (12 vs 62 cases), corresponding to 80.7% vaccine efficacy (95% CI, 64.2% to 89.6%) in the intention-to-treat analysis, demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Treatment failure, defined as a platelet count below 30×10^9/L and initiation of second-line treatment, assessed in a time-to-event analysis.
brief_rationale: The mycophenolate mofetil plus glucocorticoid group had significantly fewer primary-endpoint treatment failures than the glucocorticoid-only group (22% vs 44%; hazard ratio 0.41, 95% CI 0.21–0.80; P=0.008), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Stroke
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was stroke. Stroke rates were significantly lower with salt substitute than with regular salt (rate ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.77–0.96; P=0.006), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less often with empagliflozin than placebo (13.8% vs 17.1%; hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.69–0.90; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.
The abstract reports noninferiority and superiority comparisons but does not explicitly identify any endpoint as the prespecified primary endpoint or an unambiguous equivalent.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the mean number of migraine days per month across the 12-week treatment period.
brief_rationale: All three atogepant doses produced significantly greater reductions in monthly migraine days than placebo, with mean differences of -1.2, -1.4, and -1.7 days and P<0.001 for each comparison, meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Organ support-free days through day 21, measured on an ordinal scale combining in-hospital death and days free of cardiovascular or respiratory organ support among survivors to discharge.
brief_rationale: The trial was stopped after the prespecified superiority criterion was met. Therapeutic-dose anticoagulation had a 98.6% probability of increasing organ support-free days versus usual-care thromboprophylaxis (adjusted odds ratio 1.27; 95% credible interval 1.03 to 1.58).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of congenital CMV infection or fetal or neonatal death when CMV testing of the fetus or neonate was not performed
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 22.7% of the hyperimmune globulin group versus 19.4% of the placebo group (relative risk 1.17, 95% CI 0.80–1.72; P=0.42). Hyperimmune globulin therefore did not produce the intended lower incidence, and the trial was stopped early for futility.

primary_endpoint_description: Disease-free survival
brief_rationale: The 5-year extension did not improve the explicitly identified primary endpoint of disease-free survival versus the 2-year extension (335 events in each group; hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.85–1.15; P=0.90), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Symptomatic virologically confirmed dengue of any severity caused by any dengue virus serotype
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred less often in intervention clusters than in control clusters (2.3% vs 9.4%; odds ratio 0.23, 95% CI 0.15–0.35; P=0.004), demonstrating statistically significant benefit in the intended direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Infant survival to NICU discharge and survival without oxygen supplementation at 6 months of age.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary outcomes failed to show significant superiority of FETO over expectant care: survival to discharge had P=0.06, and survival without oxygen supplementation at 6 months had a 95% CI for the relative risk that included 1.

primary_endpoint_description: Invasive disease-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored olaparib over placebo (hazard ratio for invasive disease or death, 0.58; 99.5% CI, 0.41–0.82; P<0.001), demonstrating significant superiority at the prespecified interim analysis.

primary_endpoint_description: Disease-free survival in the intention-to-treat population and in patients with tumor PD-L1 expression of at least 1%.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored nivolumab over placebo: HR 0.70 (98.22% CI 0.55–0.90; P<0.001) in the intention-to-treat population and HR 0.55 (98.72% CI 0.35–0.85; P<0.001) in the PD-L1 ≥1% population.

The abstract reports a noninferiority immunogenicity objective, safety, and efficacy outcomes, but it does not explicitly identify any endpoint as the prespecified primary endpoint or an unambiguous equivalent.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of myocardial infarction, other acute coronary syndromes, stroke, acute decompensated heart failure, or death from cardiovascular causes
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite outcome occurred significantly less often with intensive than standard blood-pressure control (1.77% vs 2.40% per year; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.63–0.86), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin scale score of 0 to 3 at 90 days
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 44.2% with endovascular therapy versus 37.7% with medical care (risk ratio 1.18, 95% CI 0.92–1.50), and the groups did not differ significantly; therefore, favorable superiority was not established.

primary_endpoint_description: Short Physical Performance Battery score at 3 months
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored rehabilitation over usual care: adjusted mean scores were 8.3 versus 6.9, with a between-group difference of 1.5 (95% CI, 0.9 to 2.0; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean number (rate) of acute otitis media episodes per child-year during a 2-year period
brief_rationale: The intention-to-treat primary outcome rate was 1.48 episodes per child-year with tympanostomy tubes versus 1.56 with medical management (P=0.66), so tympanostomy-tube placement did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Survival free of tuberculosis at 12 months
brief_rationale: Using the prespecified 6.6-percentage-point noninferiority margin, the 4-month rifapentine–moxifloxacin regimen was noninferior to the standard 6-month regimen; the upper 95% CI bounds were below the margin in both analysis populations. The rifapentine regimen without moxifloxacin did not demonstrate noninferiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Postpartum hemorrhage, defined as calculated estimated blood loss greater than 1000 mL or receipt of a red-cell transfusion within 2 days after delivery.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome was significantly less frequent with tranexamic acid than placebo (26.7% vs 31.6%; adjusted risk ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.75–0.94; P=0.003), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Vaccine efficacy against moderate to severe-critical Covid-19 with onset at least 14 days and at least 28 days after vaccination in the SARS-CoV-2-negative per-protocol population.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored Ad26.COV2.S: efficacy was 66.9% at ≥14 days (adjusted 95% CI, 59.0–73.4) and 66.1% at ≥28 days (adjusted 95% CI, 55.0–74.8), with confidence intervals excluding no efficacy.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the 16-item Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology–Self-Report (QIDS-SR-16) score at week 6
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint showed no significant favorable difference between psilocybin and escitalopram (between-group difference 2.0 points; 95% CI, -5.0 to 0.9; P=0.17), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: ACR20 response at week 12 with each upadacitinib dose compared with placebo
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was met: ACR20 response rates were 70.6% with 15-mg and 78.5% with 30-mg upadacitinib versus 36.2% with placebo, with P<0.001 for both comparisons.

primary_endpoint_description: Safety and vaccine efficacy against laboratory-confirmed symptomatic Covid-19 more than 14 days after the second dose.
brief_rationale: The abstract identifies safety and efficacy as primary endpoints. Efficacy was 21.9% (95% CI, -49.9 to 59.8), which did not establish favorable superiority, while serious adverse events were balanced. No overall success rule combining the safety and efficacy endpoints is stated.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) score at 76 weeks.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored donanemab over placebo: the mean iADRS change was -6.86 versus -10.06, a between-group difference of 3.20 points (95% CI, 0.12 to 6.27; P=0.04), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Verified reversal of hepatorenal syndrome, defined as two consecutive serum creatinine measurements of 1.5 mg/dL or less at least 2 hours apart, with survival without renal-replacement therapy for at least 10 days after treatment completion.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred in 32% of the terlipressin group versus 17% of the placebo group (P=0.006), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Respiratory and cardiovascular organ support-free days through day 21, measured on an ordinal scale combining in-hospital death (assigned -1) and days free of organ support
brief_rationale: Both tocilizumab and sarilumab met the predefined efficacy criteria for the explicitly identified primary outcome. Versus control, adjusted cumulative odds ratios were 1.64 and 1.76, with posterior probabilities of superiority greater than 99.9% and 99.5%, respectively, in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. Enfortumab vedotin significantly improved overall survival versus chemotherapy (median 12.88 vs 8.97 months; hazard ratio for death 0.70, 95% CI 0.56–0.89; P=0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints: percentage change in body weight from baseline to week 68 and achievement of at least 5% weight reduction at week 68.
brief_rationale: Both coprimary endpoints favored semaglutide over placebo: mean weight change was -14.9% versus -2.4% (difference -12.4 percentage points; P<0.001), and 86.4% versus 31.5% achieved at least 5% weight loss (P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Positive urine pregnancy test 1 month after IUD insertion
brief_rationale: The between-group pregnancy-rate difference was 0.3 percentage points (95% CI, -0.9 to 1.8), with the upper confidence bound below the prespecified 2.5-percentage-point noninferiority margin; therefore, levonorgestrel IUD met the primary noninferiority criterion versus copper IUD.

primary_endpoint_description: Response, defined as at least three methamphetamine-negative urine samples out of four obtained at the end of stage 1 or stage 2, analyzed as the weighted average response across both stages.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored naltrexone-bupropion: weighted response was 13.6% versus 2.5% with placebo, an 11.1-percentage-point treatment effect (Wald z=4.53; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Favorable outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 3 at 6 months after randomization
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred less often with dexamethasone than placebo (83.9% vs 90.3%; difference −6.4 percentage points, 95% CI −11.4 to −1.4; P=0.01), a statistically significant result favoring placebo rather than dexamethasone.

The abstract reports all-cause mortality as the single endpoint of an unplanned interim analysis, but it does not explicitly identify or report the trial's prespecified primary endpoint. The focal interim endpoint cannot be assumed to be the original primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: PCR-confirmed, symptomatic Covid-19 within 14 days
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 5.7% of hydroxychloroquine recipients and 6.2% of usual-care recipients (risk ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.52–1.42), so hydroxychloroquine did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints of progression-free survival and overall survival.
brief_rationale: Pembrolizumab was superior for progression-free survival (HR 0.60; P=0.0002), but overall-survival data were immature and remained blinded. The abstract does not state the overall success rule for the two primary endpoints.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical status 30 days after intervention, measured on a six-point ordinal scale from total recovery to death
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome showed no significant favorable difference between convalescent plasma and placebo (odds ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.52–1.35; P=0.46), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored lorlatinib over crizotinib, with a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.28 (95% CI, 0.19–0.41; P<0.001), demonstrating significantly longer progression-free survival.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of the total number of deaths from cardiovascular causes, hospitalizations for heart failure, and urgent visits for heart failure
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred at 5.6 versus 7.5 events per 100 patient-years with sotagliflozin versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.63–0.88; P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to the first pericarditis recurrence during the randomized-withdrawal period
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored rilonacept: hazard ratio 0.04 (95% CI, 0.01–0.18) versus placebo, with P<0.001 by the log-rank test, demonstrating a significantly lower recurrence risk.

primary_endpoint_description: First documented recurrence of any atrial tachyarrhythmia (atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia) between days 91 and 365 after catheter ablation or initiation of antiarrhythmic drug therapy.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred less often with cryoballoon ablation than with antiarrhythmic drugs (42.9% vs 67.8%; hazard ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.35–0.66; P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to intubation or death
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was intubation or death in a time-to-event analysis. Tocilizumab did not show favorable superiority over placebo (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.38–1.81; P=0.64), so the primary endpoint did not meet the success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: 30-day health status assessed with the EQ-5D questionnaire, using a noninferiority margin of 0.05 points
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies 30-day EQ-5D health status as the primary outcome and reports that antibiotics were noninferior to appendectomy (mean difference 0.01 points; 95% CI, -0.001 to 0.03), satisfying the stated 0.05-point noninferiority margin.

primary_endpoint_description: Major adverse cardiovascular events, defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
brief_rationale: The prespecified primary objective was noninferiority to placebo with an upper hazard-ratio confidence bound margin of 1.3. The hazard ratio was 0.97 (95.6% CI, 0.85–1.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority), satisfying the criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in glycated hemoglobin level from baseline to week 26
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint was explicitly identified and showed an estimated between-group difference of -0.18 percentage points (95% CI, -0.38 to 0.02; P=0.08). However, the abstract does not specify a superiority, noninferiority, or equivalence success criterion, so whether the primary endpoint met the prespecified criterion cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Investigator-assessed disease-free survival among patients with stage II to IIIA EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored osimertinib: the hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death was 0.17 (99.06% CI, 0.11–0.26; P<0.001), demonstrating significantly longer disease-free survival than with placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy renal response at week 104: urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio ≤0.7, qualifying eGFR preservation/threshold, and no rescue therapy.
brief_rationale: The primary response occurred in 43% with belimumab versus 32% with placebo (odds ratio 1.6, 95% CI 1.0–2.3; P=0.03), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the alveolar-arterial difference in oxygen concentration (A-aDo2) at week 24
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint improved significantly more with continuous molgramostim than with placebo (-12.8 vs -6.6 mm Hg; estimated treatment difference, -6.2 mm Hg; P=0.03), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to the first bronchiectasis exacerbation during the 24-week treatment period
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was time to first exacerbation. Both brensocatib doses significantly prolonged this endpoint versus placebo, with hazard ratios of 0.58 (P=0.03) for 10 mg and 0.62 (P=0.046) for 25 mg, demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Reactogenicity; laboratory safety values (serum chemistry and hematology using FDA toxicity scoring); and IgG anti-spike protein response at the day-35 primary analysis.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies several primary safety and immunogenicity outcomes and reports generally favorable findings, but it does not state a prespecified threshold or overall success rule for determining whether these outcomes met trial success.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiovascular death, spontaneous (nonprocedural) myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or ischemia-driven coronary revascularization.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred less often with colchicine than placebo (6.8% vs 9.6%; hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.57–0.83; P<0.001), demonstrating statistically significant benefit in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Two primary outcomes over 12 months: all bleeding and non-procedure-related bleeding.
brief_rationale: Both primary bleeding outcomes significantly favored aspirin alone over aspirin plus clopidogrel: all bleeding was 15.1% vs 26.6% (risk ratio 0.57; P=0.001), and non-procedure-related bleeding was 15.1% vs 24.9% (risk ratio 0.61; P=0.005).

primary_endpoint_description: Percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol level at week 24
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored evinacumab: LDL cholesterol decreased by 47.1% versus a 1.9% increase with placebo, yielding a between-group difference of -49.0 percentage points (95% CI, -65.0 to -33.1; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Primary safety outcomes were adverse events within 1 hour after infusion and throughout the trial; the primary efficacy outcome was the TY014 dose at which 100% of participants were negative for viremia within 48 hours.
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy target was achieved at 2 mg/kg, with all 5 recipients aviremic at 48 hours. However, the publication also identifies primary safety outcomes without specifying a criterion for their success or an overall rule integrating the safety and efficacy outcomes, so overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Fibroid-related quality of life at 2 years, assessed by the health-related quality-of-life domain score of the UFS-QOL questionnaire and adjusted for baseline score.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored myomectomy: adjusted mean difference 8.0 points (95% CI, 1.8 to 14.1; P=0.01), with higher scores indicating better quality of life. The imputed analysis also favored myomectomy (difference 6.5; 95% CI, 1.1 to 11.9), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: RSV-associated, medically significant lower respiratory tract infection in infants through 90 days of life
brief_rationale: The prespecified success criterion required the lower bound of the 97.52% confidence interval for vaccine efficacy to be at least 30%. Vaccine efficacy was 39.4%, but the 97.52% CI was -1.0% to 63.7%, so the primary endpoint did not meet the criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection through 150 days after dose administration
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred in 2.6% of nirsevimab recipients versus 9.5% of placebo recipients, a favorable 70.1% reduction (95% CI, 52.3% to 81.2%; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean percent change from baseline to week 16 in the visual-analogue scale score for pruritus
brief_rationale: Nemolizumab produced a significantly greater reduction in pruritus VAS score than placebo (-42.8% vs -21.4%; difference, -21.5 percentage points; 95% CI, -30.2 to -12.7; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical influenza confirmed by reverse-transcriptase polymerase-chain-reaction testing over 10 days
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred significantly less often with baloxavir than placebo (1.9% vs 13.6%; adjusted risk ratio 0.14, 95% CI 0.06–0.30; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from randomization to week 104
brief_rationale: The primary outcome did not differ significantly between allopurinol and placebo (mean between-group difference, -0.10 ml/min/1.73 m² per year; 95% CI, -1.18 to 0.97; P=0.85), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Modified Rankin scale score at 90 days
brief_rationale: The primary outcome favored thrombectomy, with a common odds ratio for a better modified Rankin scale distribution of 2.28 (95% CI, 1.41–3.69; P=0.001); the trial was stopped early for efficacy.

primary_endpoint_description: Event-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was event-free survival. Three-year event-free survival was 93.9% with rituximab plus chemotherapy versus 82.3% with chemotherapy alone (hazard ratio 0.32, 95% CI 0.15–0.66; one-sided P=0.00096), explicitly reaching the required significance level in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of either laboratory-confirmed Covid-19 or illness compatible with Covid-19 within 14 days
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 11.8% of hydroxychloroquine recipients versus 14.3% of placebo recipients; the difference was not statistically significant (absolute difference −2.4 percentage points, 95% CI −7.0 to 2.2; P=0.35), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints of overall survival and independently assessed progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: Both coprimary endpoints significantly favored atezolizumab plus bevacizumab over sorafenib: overall survival HR 0.58 (95% CI, 0.42–0.79; P<0.001) and progression-free survival HR 0.59 (95% CI, 0.47–0.76; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Imaging-based progression-free survival in cohort A according to blinded independent central review
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored olaparib: median imaging-based progression-free survival was 7.4 versus 3.6 months, with a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.34 (95% CI, 0.25–0.47; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in BMI standard-deviation score at week 56
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored liraglutide over placebo, with an estimated difference of -0.22 (95% CI, -0.37 to -0.08; P=0.002), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death or nonfatal myocardial infarction
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred at similar estimated 3-year rates with the invasive and conservative strategies (36.4% vs 36.7%; adjusted hazard ratio 1.01, 95% CI 0.79–1.29; P=0.95), so the invasive strategy did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

This is a secondary health-status analysis. Although the SAQ summary score is called the primary outcome of this analysis, health status is explicitly described as a secondary trial objective. The original trial’s prespecified primary endpoint is not explicitly identified and sufficiently reported in the supplied abstract.

primary_endpoint_description: Major venous thromboembolism, a composite of symptomatic distal or proximal deep-vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, venous thromboembolism-related death during treatment, or asymptomatic proximal deep-vein thrombosis at the end of treatment.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy outcome occurred in 0.2% with rivaroxaban versus 1.1% with enoxaparin. The prespecified noninferiority criterion was met (P<0.001), and the planned subsequent superiority test also favored rivaroxaban (P=0.01).

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage of participants with an HIV-1 RNA level of 50 copies/mL or higher at week 48 (FDA snapshot algorithm).
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 2.1% with long-acting therapy versus 2.5% with oral therapy (adjusted difference, -0.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.8 to 2.1), explicitly meeting the prespecified 6-percentage-point noninferiority margin.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death from any cause or end-stage kidney disease
brief_rationale: The factorial trial evaluated the same primary composite outcome under two primary hypotheses: plasma exchange was not superior to control (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.65–1.13; P=0.27), whereas reduced-dose glucocorticoids met noninferiority versus standard dose. With mixed results and no stated overall success rule, a single trial-level result is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Safety composite of death from cardiac causes, myocardial infarction, or stent thrombosis at 1 year
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 17.1% versus 16.9%. The upper boundary of the one-sided 97.5% CI for the risk difference was 3.5 percentage points, below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 4.1 points (P=0.01 for noninferiority), so the primary noninferiority criterion was met.

This follow-up abstract evaluates 6-year asthma and recurrent wheeze but does not explicitly identify an endpoint as the trial's prespecified primary endpoint. Therefore, the reported absence of effect cannot be definitively classified as the primary-endpoint result.

primary_endpoint_description: Development of gastric cancer
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less often with H. pylori eradication therapy than with placebo (1.2% vs. 2.7%; hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.21–0.94; log-rank P=0.03), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Lung reexpansion within 8 weeks
brief_rationale: In the complete-case primary analysis, the risk difference was -4.1 percentage points (95% CI, -8.6 to 0.5); the lower CI bound remained within the prespecified -9-point noninferiority margin (P=0.02 for noninferiority). A conservative missing-data sensitivity analysis did not confirm noninferiority, but the reported primary analysis met the stated criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Proptosis response, defined as a reduction in proptosis of at least 2 mm, at week 24.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored teprotumumab: 83% achieved a proptosis response versus 10% with placebo (P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Oropharyngeal carriage of disease-causing Neisseria meningitidis (groups A, B, C, W, X, or Y) at 12 months in students in years 10 and 11
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome did not differ favorably between vaccination and control groups (2.55% vs 2.52%; adjusted odds ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.80–1.31; P=0.85), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death or severe neurodevelopmental impairment at 22 to 26 months of postmenstrual age
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 26% of both the erythropoietin and placebo groups (relative risk 1.03, 95% CI 0.81–1.32; P=0.80). Erythropoietin therefore did not achieve favorable superiority by lowering the risk of the primary outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: Red-cell transfusion independence for 8 weeks or longer during weeks 1 through 24
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred in 38% of luspatercept-treated patients versus 13% of placebo-treated patients, a favorable and statistically significant difference (P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

The abstract reports a protocol-specified interim analysis of overall survival and mentions an earlier progression-free survival analysis, but it does not explicitly identify either outcome as the trial's prespecified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death during or within 30 days after surgery (operative mortality) or cardiovascular death during follow-up
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 1% with early surgery versus 15% with conservative care (hazard ratio 0.09, 95% CI 0.01–0.67; P=0.003), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: 6-month mortality
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was 6-month mortality. Mortality was higher with high-dose rifampin than with standard-dose rifampin (44.6% vs. 40.7%; hazard ratio 1.17, 95% CI 0.89–1.54; P=0.25), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: In-hospital death from any cause by day 28
brief_rationale: Mortality was 28.1% with ketamine versus 29.1% with etomidate (adjusted risk difference, -0.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.5 to 2.9; P=0.65). Ketamine therefore did not achieve significantly lower mortality on the explicitly identified primary outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: Frequency and severity of adverse events
brief_rationale: The primary outcomes were explicitly identified as adverse-event frequency and severity and were reported descriptively, but no prespecified criterion defining primary-endpoint success was provided.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months compared with baseline
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored sibeprenlimab: the adjusted geometric least-squares mean urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was 51.2% lower than with placebo (96.5% CI, 42.9% to 58.2; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Percent change in triglyceride level at 6 months, expressed as the placebo-adjusted change for each olezarsen dose group
brief_rationale: In both trials, both olezarsen doses produced significantly greater triglyceride reductions than placebo at 6 months, with placebo-adjusted changes ranging from -49.2 to -72.2 percentage points (P<0.001 for all comparisons), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Prostate cancer mortality
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was prostate cancer mortality. Screening reduced prostate cancer mortality by 13% versus control (rate ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.80 to 0.95), with the confidence interval excluding no effect in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review.
brief_rationale: At the prespecified interim analysis, trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab improved progression-free survival versus THP (median 40.7 vs 26.9 months; hazard ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.44–0.71). The P value was <0.00001, crossing the prespecified superiority boundary of 0.00043.

primary_endpoint_description: Death from any cause at 30 days after enrollment
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored adjunctive glucocorticoids: 30-day mortality was 22.6% versus 26.0% with standard care (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.73–0.97; P=0.02), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrence-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival. Nivolumab produced longer recurrence-free survival than ipilimumab (median 61.1 vs 24.2 months; hazard ratio for recurrence or death, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.63–0.90), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Death within 3 months after eligibility confirmation, analyzed in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: Neither azithromycin regimen showed favorable superiority over placebo for the primary mortality endpoint: incidence rate ratio 1.00 (95% CI, 0.83–1.19) for twice-yearly dosing and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.75–1.15) for quarterly dosing. The conclusion states that mortality was not lower than with placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Laboratory-confirmed, symptomatic Aedes-borne disease (chikungunya, dengue, or Zika)
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint was evaluated, but cumulative incidence was not significantly lower with targeted indoor residual spraying. The per-protocol efficacy estimate was -12.8% (95% CI, -60.7 to 23.0), and the intention-to-treat estimate was 3.9% (95% CI, -28.1 to 26.7), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Time-to-event colorectal cancer recurrence among patients with prespecified PIK3CA hotspot mutations in exon 9 or 20 (group A alterations).
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored aspirin: 3-year cumulative recurrence was 7.7% with aspirin versus 14.1% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.24–0.98; P=0.04), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Two ranked primary outcomes through 12 months: (1) composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or urgent target-vessel revascularization, tested for noninferiority; and (2) major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding, tested for superiority.
brief_rationale: The ischemic composite did not meet the 2.5-percentage-point noninferiority criterion (risk difference 1.47 points; 95% CI, -0.16 to 3.10; P=0.11), whereas bleeding favored monotherapy (risk difference -2.97 points; 95% CI, -4.20 to -1.73). The abstract does not state the overall success rule for these mixed ranked primary outcomes.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in peak oxygen uptake at week 24
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored aficamten: the least-squares mean between-group difference in change in peak oxygen uptake was 2.3 ml/kg/min (95% CI, 1.5 to 3.1; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Hospitalization for RSV-related respiratory tract disease
brief_rationale: The prespecified success criterion was vaccine effectiveness greater than 20%. The primary endpoint occurred in 3 vaccine recipients versus 18 controls, with vaccine effectiveness of 83.3% (95% CI, 42.9% to 96.9%; P=0.007 for minimum effectiveness >20%), meeting the criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to first occurrence of documented sustained ventricular tachycardia or appropriate ICD therapy, unplanned hospitalization lasting more than 24 hours for arrhythmia or heart failure, or death from any cause.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite endpoint occurred less often with the high-normal potassium strategy than with standard care (22.7% vs. 29.2%; hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.61–0.95; P=0.01), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints: undetectable measurable residual disease in bone marrow within 2 years for ibrutinib-venetoclax versus ibrutinib alone, and progression-free survival for ibrutinib-venetoclax versus FCR.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored ibrutinib-venetoclax: undetectable bone marrow MRD occurred in 66.2% versus 0% with ibrutinib alone (P<0.001), and progression or death was reduced versus FCR (HR 0.13, 95% CI 0.08–0.21; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Death at 96 hours
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was 96-hour mortality. In this superiority trial, mortality did not differ favorably between oral and intravenous rehydration (8% vs. 7%; risk ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.41–2.52; P=0.69), so superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Time from randomization to successful liberation from mechanical ventilation
brief_rationale: The primary outcome showed no favorable superiority of PAV+ over PSV: median time to successful liberation was 7.3 versus 6.8 days, respectively (P=0.58), and the difference was not statistically significant.

primary_endpoint_description: Transfusion of at least one unit of allogeneic red cells during the hospital stay
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 27.3% of the ANH group versus 29.2% of the usual-care group (relative risk 0.93, 95% CI 0.81–1.07; P=0.34), so ANH did not demonstrate a significant reduction.

primary_endpoint_description: Relative change in the log-transformed mean urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio from baseline to 180 days
brief_rationale: Combination therapy produced significantly greater reductions in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio than finerenone alone (ratio 0.71; 95% CI, 0.61–0.82; P<0.001) and empagliflozin alone (ratio 0.68; 95% CI, 0.59–0.79; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion for the stated primary outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: MRD-negative status at 10^-6 sensitivity before maintenance therapy
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint did not show favorable superiority in either randomized cohort: ASCT versus Isa-KRd yielded 86% versus 84% MRD negativity (adjusted RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95–1.10; P=0.64), and tandem versus single ASCT yielded 32% versus 40% (adjusted RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.58–1.15; P=0.31).

primary_endpoint_description: Event-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was event-free survival. Durvalumab plus FLOT improved event-free survival versus placebo plus FLOT (hazard ratio for event or death, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.58–0.86; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Disease-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was disease-free survival. Cemiplimab was superior to placebo, with a hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death of 0.32 (95% CI, 0.20–0.51; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Functional independence at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin scale score of 0 to 2.
brief_rationale: Functional independence occurred in 52.9% with tenecteplase plus thrombectomy versus 44.1% with thrombectomy alone (risk ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.01–1.43; P=0.04), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Viral load below 400 copies per milliliter at 96 weeks
brief_rationale: The single primary outcome was assessed through multiple prespecified factorial comparisons using superiority and noninferiority criteria. TAF-emtricitabine, dolutegravir, and atazanavir met their respective criteria, whereas darunavir did not meet its prespecified superiority threshold. No overall success rule for these mixed primary comparisons is stated.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean change from baseline to week 8 in average sleep latency on the Maintenance of Wakefulness Test
brief_rationale: All oveporexton regimens produced favorable increases in MWT average sleep latency versus placebo, with adjusted P≤0.001 for every comparison, meeting the superiority criterion for the explicitly identified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Reduction of at least one stage of fibrosis without worsening of MASH at week 36
brief_rationale: At week 36, neither efruxifermin dose showed significant superiority over placebo for the primary outcome (28 mg: P=0.62; 50 mg: P=0.52). Thus, the primary endpoint did not meet the success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in 24-hour average systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 12, assessed as the least-squares mean difference from placebo in each lorundrostat group.
brief_rationale: Both lorundrostat regimens produced favorable placebo-adjusted reductions at week 12, with 97.5% confidence intervals excluding zero: −7.9 mm Hg (−13.3 to −2.6) for stable dosing and −6.5 mm Hg (−11.8 to −1.2) for dose adjustment.

primary_endpoint_description: Confirmed disability progression sustained for at least 6 months, assessed in a time-to-event analysis.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored tolebrutinib over placebo (22.6% vs 30.7%; hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.55–0.88; P=0.003), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Sustained remission at week 52, defined as absence of giant-cell arteritis signs or symptoms from weeks 12 through 52 and adherence to the protocol-specified glucocorticoid taper.
brief_rationale: Upadacitinib 15 mg was superior to placebo for the primary endpoint (46.4% vs 29.0%; P=0.002), meeting the superiority criterion. The 7.5-mg dose was not superior, but the 15-mg regimen demonstrated primary-endpoint success.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline to week 12 in the 7-day urticaria activity score (UAS7)
brief_rationale: In both REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, remibrutinib produced a significantly greater favorable decrease in UAS7 than placebo at week 12 (P<0.001 in each trial), meeting the superiority criterion for the explicitly identified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Seroconversion at 28 days after vaccination for each fractional dose (1000 IU, 500 IU, and 250 IU) compared with the standard dose, assessed for noninferiority with a -10-percentage-point margin.
brief_rationale: The 1000-IU and 500-IU doses met the noninferiority criterion in both analysis populations, whereas the 250-IU dose failed it in the per-protocol analysis. Because the primary outcome involved multiple dose comparisons with mixed results and no overall trial success rule is stated, the overall primary-endpoint result is unclear.

primary_endpoint_description: Modified Rankin Scale score of 0 or 1 at 90 days
brief_rationale: The favorable primary outcome occurred in 41.6% with EVT plus usual care versus 43.1% with usual care alone (adjusted rate ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.79–1.15; P=0.61), so EVT did not demonstrate superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Favorable outcome at week 73, defined by two negative sputum cultures or favorable bacteriologic, clinical, and radiologic evolution.
brief_rationale: With a prespecified noninferiority margin of -12 percentage points, three shortened all-oral regimens had consistent modified intention-to-treat and per-protocol results supporting noninferiority to standard therapy.

primary_endpoint_description: Bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis within 30 months
brief_rationale: Confirmed tuberculosis was less frequent with levofloxacin than placebo (0.6% vs 1.1%; incidence rate ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.19–1.62), but the difference was not statistically significant; therefore, the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Disease-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was disease-free survival. Blinatumomab plus chemotherapy improved estimated 3-year disease-free survival versus chemotherapy alone (96.0% vs 87.9%; stratified log-rank P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of HIV infection in the lenacapavir group compared with background HIV incidence in the screened population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy analysis showed significantly lower HIV incidence with lenacapavir than the background incidence (incidence rate ratio, 0.04; 95% CI, 0.01–0.18; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Symptomatic recurrence or progression of subdural hematoma within 90 days after randomization
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 6.7% with embolization versus 9.9% with usual care; the between-group difference was not statistically significant (95% CI, -7.4 to 0.8 percentage points; P=0.10), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Death from any cause by 90 days after diagnosis of the bloodstream infection
brief_rationale: The prespecified primary outcome had a 4-percentage-point noninferiority margin. Mortality was 14.5% with 7 days versus 16.1% with 14 days (difference, -1.6 percentage points; 95.7% CI, -4.0 to 0.8), which the abstract explicitly states demonstrated noninferiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death from any cause during follow-up or, more than 14 days after randomization, ventricular tachycardia storm, appropriate ICD shock, or sustained ventricular tachycardia treated by medical intervention.
brief_rationale: The primary composite endpoint occurred less often with catheter ablation than with antiarrhythmic drug therapy (50.7% vs 60.6%; hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.58–0.97; P=0.03), demonstrating favorable superiority.
The abstract explicitly identifies the reported efficacy outcomes as three key secondary end points and does not identify or report a prespecified primary endpoint for this assessment.

primary_endpoint_description: Sustained return of spontaneous circulation
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 30% with initial intraosseous access versus 29% with intravenous access (risk ratio 1.06, 95% CI 0.90–1.24; P=0.49), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Hierarchical composite of all-cause death, right ventricular assist device implantation or heart transplantation, postindex tricuspid-valve intervention, heart-failure hospitalization, and improvements in KCCQ-OS score, NYHA functional class, and 6-minute walk distance
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary hierarchical composite favored transcatheter valve replacement, with a win ratio of 2.02 (95% CI, 1.56–2.62; P<0.001); the abstract states that valve replacement was superior to medical therapy for this outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death, stroke, or unplanned hospitalization for cardiovascular causes
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite endpoint occurred in 26.8% with early TAVR versus 45.3% with clinical surveillance (hazard ratio 0.50, 95% CI 0.40–0.63; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline through week 24 in the Epistaxis Severity Score
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored pomalidomide, with a between-group difference of -0.94 points (95% CI, -1.57 to -0.31; P=0.004). This exceeded the stated clinically significant reduction of 0.71 points, and the planned interim analysis met the prespecified efficacy threshold.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall response (complete or partial response) during the first six treatment cycles
brief_rationale: Success required the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for overall response to exceed 30%. This criterion was met in all three dose groups, with lower bounds of 63%, 55%, and 39%, respectively.

primary_endpoint_description: Event-free survival was one of two primary end points; the other primary end point is not identified in the abstract.
brief_rationale: Event-free survival significantly favored durvalumab (hazard ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.56–0.82; P<0.001), but the abstract states that there were two primary end points without identifying or reporting the other or specifying the overall success rule.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review among patients with HER2-low disease.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored trastuzumab deruxtecan over chemotherapy: median progression-free survival was 13.2 versus 8.1 months, with a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.62 (95% CI, 0.52–0.75; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to first hospitalization or death from any cause within 1 year
brief_rationale: The trial explicitly tested nonsuperiority of 24-hour versus 15-hour oxygen therapy for the primary composite endpoint. The hazard ratio was 0.99 (90% CI, 0.76–1.29), with P=0.007 for nonsuperiority, meeting the stated intended success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Utility-weighted 90-day modified Rankin scale score, with higher scores indicating better outcomes.
brief_rationale: Neither adjunctive argatroban nor eptifibatide demonstrated superiority to placebo on the primary efficacy outcome. Mean scores were lower with both active treatments, and posterior probabilities of being better than placebo were 0.002 and 0.041, respectively.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of total worsening heart failure events (first or recurrent unplanned hospitalization or urgent visit for heart failure) and death from cardiovascular causes
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred at a significantly lower rate with finerenone than placebo (rate ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.74–0.95; P=0.007), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.
The abstract reports HIV-incidence efficacy comparisons for lenacapavir and F/TAF but does not explicitly identify any endpoint as the prespecified primary endpoint or an unambiguous equivalent.

primary_endpoint_description: Sequential primary endpoints: clinical remission at week 24, tested for noninferiority with a 10-percentage-point margin, and endoscopic remission at week 48, tested for superiority.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly states that both primary endpoints were met. Risankizumab was noninferior to ustekinumab for week-24 clinical remission (adjusted difference 18.4 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.6 to 30.3) and superior for week-48 endoscopic remission (adjusted difference 15.6 percentage points; 95% CI, 8.4 to 22.9; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy outcome: clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding in the ICU at 90 days; primary safety outcome: death from any cause at 90 days.
brief_rationale: Pantoprazole significantly reduced the primary efficacy outcome (1.0% vs 3.5%; HR 0.30, P<0.001), while the primary safety outcome showed no significant mortality difference (HR 0.94, P=0.25). The abstract does not specify an overall success rule or criterion for the safety outcome, so overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored isatuximab-VRd over VRd, with a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.60 (98.5% CI, 0.41–0.88; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Event-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was event-free survival. Neoadjuvant ipilimumab plus nivolumab significantly prolonged event-free survival versus surgery followed by adjuvant nivolumab (hazard ratio 0.32, 99.9% CI 0.15–0.66; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Percent change in daily glucocorticoid dose from baseline to week 24 while maintaining androstenedione control
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored crinecerfont: glucocorticoid dose decreased by 27.3% versus 10.3% with placebo, with a least-squares mean difference of -17.0 percentage points (P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Major kidney disease events: a composite of kidney failure, at least a 50% reduction in eGFR from baseline, or death from kidney-related or cardiovascular causes.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less often with semaglutide than placebo (331 vs. 410 first events; hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.66–0.88; P=0.0003), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized rate of participant-initiated health care utilization for respiratory illness
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary-outcome event rate was significantly lower with the intervention than with usual care (0.53 vs. 1.12 events per person-year; incidence rate ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.36–0.63; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Modified Rankin scale score at 90 days
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored thrombectomy: median modified Rankin score was 4 versus 6 with medical care alone, with a generalized odds ratio of 1.63 (95% CI, 1.29–2.06; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Disease-free survival, tested hierarchically first among patients with stage II or IIIA disease and then in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Alectinib significantly improved the explicitly identified primary endpoint versus chemotherapy in the first hierarchical population (HR for recurrence or death, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.13–0.45; P<0.001) and subsequently in the intention-to-treat population (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.13–0.43; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death from any cause or fatal or nonfatal stroke at 1 year
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 5.4% of the TAVI group versus 10.0% of the SAVR group (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.35–0.79), with P<0.001 for noninferiority; thus, the prespecified noninferiority criterion was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Hierarchically assessed differences versus placebo in percent change in fasting triglyceride level from baseline to 6 months for olezarsen 80 mg and, if significant, olezarsen 50 mg.
brief_rationale: The 80-mg comparison was significant and favorable (-43.5 percentage points; P<0.001), whereas the gated 50-mg comparison was not significant (-22.4 percentage points; P=0.08). The abstract does not specify the overall success rule for these mixed primary-endpoint results.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause, assessed in a time-to-first-event analysis.
brief_rationale: The primary composite endpoint was not significantly reduced with empagliflozin versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.76–1.06; P=0.21), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Two primary endpoints in the randomized first trial: hemoglobin increase of at least 2 g/dL from baseline without red-cell transfusion, and hemoglobin level of at least 12 g/dL without red-cell transfusion.
brief_rationale: Both primary endpoints favored iptacopan: 51/60 and 42/60 iptacopan-treated patients achieved the respective endpoints versus 0/35 continuing anti-C5 therapy. The abstract explicitly states that iptacopan showed superiority to anti-C5 therapy.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints of progression-free survival by blinded independent central review and overall survival
