primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy composite of recurrent or residual chronic subdural hematoma, reoperation or surgical rescue, or major disabling stroke, myocardial infarction, or neurologic death within 180 days; and primary safety composite of major disabling stroke or death from any cause within 30 days.
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy outcome significantly favored embolization (16% vs 36%; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.20–0.66; P=0.001). A separate primary safety outcome occurred in 3% of each group, but no prespecified safety criterion or overall rule combining the two primary outcomes is reported, so overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Two primary endpoints: (1) time to first adjudicated cardiovascular death or worsening heart-failure event and (2) change from baseline to 52 weeks in KCCQ clinical summary score.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored tirzepatide and were statistically significant: the cardiovascular death/worsening heart-failure composite was reduced (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41–0.95; P=0.026), and KCCQ-CSS improved versus placebo (difference 6.9 points, 95% CI 3.3–10.6; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Two primary outcomes: (1) total events of cardiovascular death or new/worsening heart failure; and (2) first occurrence of myocardial infarction, stroke, new/worsening heart failure, or cardiovascular death.
brief_rationale: Neither primary outcome showed significant benefit with spironolactone versus placebo: HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.69–1.21; P=0.51) for the first and HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.81–1.13; P=0.60) for the second.

primary_endpoint_description: Survival at 30 days
brief_rationale: The intraosseous-first strategy did not improve the explicitly identified primary outcome of 30-day survival versus the intravenous-first strategy (4.5% vs 5.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.94, 95% CI 0.68–1.32; P=0.74), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored inavolisib: median progression-free survival was 15.0 versus 7.3 months, with a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.43 (95% CI, 0.32–0.59; P<0.001), demonstrating significant superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio from baseline to week 36 in the first 270 patients in the main stratum
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored atrasentan: the geometric mean percentage change was -38.1% with atrasentan versus -3.1% with placebo, with a between-group difference of -36.1 percentage points (95% CI, -44.6 to -26.4; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death from the start of the active-trial period through the end of post-trial follow-up.
brief_rationale: The primary composite outcome occurred in 26.2% of the empagliflozin group versus 30.3% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.72–0.87), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival, defined as time from randomization to progressive disease or death from any cause.
brief_rationale: At the planned interim analysis, N+AVD crossed the efficacy threshold and significantly improved the primary endpoint versus BV+AVD (hazard ratio 0.48, 99% CI 0.27–0.87; two-sided P=0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical remission at week 12 in cohort 1
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was clinical remission at week 12 in cohort 1. Remission was significantly more frequent with tulisokibart than placebo (26% vs. 1%; difference 25 percentage points, 95% CI 14 to 37; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Detection of clinically insignificant (ISUP grade 1) prostate cancer
brief_rationale: The MRI-targeted biopsy strategy significantly reduced detection of the explicitly identified primary outcome versus systematic biopsy (relative risk, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.32–0.57; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in body weight at 12 weeks
brief_rationale: All three ponsegromab dose groups had significantly greater weight gain than placebo at 12 weeks, with positive between-group differences and 95% credible intervals excluding zero, meeting the favorable superiority criterion for the explicitly identified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint was overall survival. Preoperative chemoradiotherapy did not significantly improve overall survival versus perioperative chemotherapy alone (median 46 vs. 49 months; hazard ratio for death, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.83–1.31), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized rate of asthma exacerbations at 52 weeks
brief_rationale: In both replicate placebo-controlled trials, depemokimab significantly reduced the explicitly identified primary endpoint: rate ratios were 0.42 in SWIFT-1 and 0.52 in SWIFT-2, with P<0.001 for both, demonstrating favorable superiority over placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy endpoint: stroke or systemic embolism (noninferiority of asundexian to apixaban); primary safety endpoint: major bleeding (superiority of asundexian to apixaban).
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy objective was not met and favored apixaban (HR 3.79, 95% CI 2.46–5.83), whereas the primary safety objective favored asundexian (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.18–0.55). The abstract does not state an overall success rule for these mixed primary objectives.

primary_endpoint_description: Median percent change from baseline in fasting triglyceride level at 10 months.
brief_rationale: At 10 months, median fasting triglyceride levels decreased by 80% and 78% with plozasiran 25 mg and 50 mg, respectively, versus 17% with placebo; the favorable between-group result was statistically significant (P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiovascular death, stroke from any cause, myocardial infarction, major vascular complications, or major bleeding within 30 days after TAVI
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 16.5% with continuation versus 14.8% with interruption (risk difference 1.7 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.1 to 6.6; P=0.18 for noninferiority). Continuation did not meet the noninferiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Major adverse cardiac event, defined as a composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or urgent revascularization
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred less often with PCI than with conservative treatment (26% vs. 36%; hazard ratio 0.71, 95% CI 0.51–0.99; P=0.04), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Three primary community-level mortality outcomes (deaths per 1000 person-years), each involving a different age group and pairwise treatment-group comparison.
brief_rationale: The abstract identifies three primary outcomes but does not state an overall multiplicity/success rule. Reported results are mixed: mortality was significantly lower for azithromycin given to children 1–59 months versus placebo, whereas mortality was not significantly lower for treatment limited to infants 1–11 months versus placebo; the third primary outcome is not fully reported.

primary_endpoint_description: Development of symptomatic, test-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection through day 14 among participants with a negative baseline RT-PCR test
brief_rationale: Neither the 5-day nor the 10-day nirmatrelvir-ritonavir regimen significantly reduced the primary endpoint versus placebo (P=0.17 and P=0.12, respectively), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. Tisotumab vedotin significantly prolonged median overall survival versus chemotherapy (11.5 vs. 9.5 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.54–0.89; two-sided P=0.004), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Histologic remission at week 16, defined as a peak esophageal intraepithelial eosinophil count of ≤6 per high-power field.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred significantly more often with both higher-exposure dupilumab (68% vs 3%; difference 65 percentage points, 95% CI 48 to 81; P<0.001) and lower-exposure dupilumab (58% vs 3%; difference 55 percentage points, 95% CI 37 to 73; P<0.001) than with placebo at week 16.

The abstract reports overall survival, melanoma-specific survival, relapse-free survival, and distant metastasis-free survival, but does not explicitly identify any of them as the prespecified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Number of opioid-related overdose deaths among community adults during the comparison period
brief_rationale: The intervention did not significantly reduce the explicitly identified primary outcome versus control: 47.2 versus 51.7 deaths per 100,000, adjusted rate ratio 0.91 (95% CI, 0.76–1.09; P=0.30). Thus, the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin scale score 0 or 1) at 90 days
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy outcome occurred in 79.5% with reteplase versus 70.4% with alteplase (risk ratio 1.13, 95% CI 1.05–1.21), meeting the noninferiority criterion (P<0.001) and subsequently showing superiority (P=0.002).

primary_endpoint_description: Absence of disability, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 or 1 at day 90.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored tenecteplase over standard medical treatment (33.0% vs 24.2%; relative rate 1.37, 95% CI 1.04–1.81; P=0.03), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Hypoxemia during intubation, defined as oxygen saturation below 85% from induction of anesthesia through 2 minutes after tracheal intubation.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred less often with noninvasive ventilation than with an oxygen mask (9.1% vs 18.5%; difference, -9.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -13.2 to -5.6; P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was progression-free survival. BPd significantly improved progression-free survival versus PVd (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.37–0.73; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to the beginning of symptom relief, defined as a Patient Global Impression of Change rating of "a little better" at two or more consecutive time points within 12 hours after the first dose.
brief_rationale: Both sebetralstat doses produced significantly faster onset of symptom relief than placebo (300 mg: P<0.001; 600 mg: P=0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion for the explicitly identified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Safety and side-effect profile of felzartamab
brief_rationale: The primary outcome was explicitly identified as safety and side-effect profile, and adverse events were reported. However, the abstract does not state a prespecified quantitative or comparative criterion defining success; the conclusion that safety was acceptable is insufficient to determine whether a prespecified success criterion was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Functional status measured by the modified Rankin Scale at 90 days after randomization (primary efficacy outcome).
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy outcome showed no favorable difference with prehospital blood-pressure reduction versus usual care (common odds ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15), so superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Hemostatic efficacy at 12 hours, defined by hematoma-volume expansion of 35% or less, an NIH Stroke Scale increase of less than 7 points, and no rescue therapy between 3 and 12 hours.
brief_rationale: Hemostatic efficacy was achieved in 67.0% of the andexanet group versus 53.1% of the usual-care group, an adjusted favorable difference of 13.4 percentage points (95% CI, 4.6 to 22.2; P=0.003), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to first Plasmodium falciparum infection detected by blood smear performed at least every 2 weeks for 24 weeks
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored L9LS over placebo at both doses: efficacy was 66% for 150 mg and 70% for 300 mg, with P<0.001 for both comparisons.

primary_endpoint_description: Body-fat percentage at 4 months of corrected gestational age for the parenteral-nutrition and milk-supplement interventions, and time to full enteral feeding for the taste-and-smell intervention.
brief_rationale: All explicitly identified primary outcomes were similar between intervention and comparator groups: body-fat percentage showed no significant benefit for parenteral nutrition (P=0.72) or milk supplementation (P=0.25), and taste-and-smell exposure did not improve time to full enteral feeding (P=0.59). Thus, none of the superiority comparisons met the success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Hospitalization for any cause at 1 year
brief_rationale: The intervention did not reduce the explicitly identified primary outcome: hospitalization occurred in 20.7% of the intervention group versus 21.1% with usual care (between-group difference 0.4 percentage points; P=0.58), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline to 12 months in MDS-UPDRS part III score, assessed in the on-medication state
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored lixisenatide: the score changed by -0.04 points with lixisenatide versus +3.04 points with placebo, for a between-group difference of 3.08 points (95% CI, 0.86 to 5.30; P=0.007), demonstrating significantly less progression of motor disability.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies overall survival as the primary endpoint but reports only the prespecified secondary endpoint of recurrence-free survival. Therefore, the primary endpoint's noninferiority result cannot be assessed.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or unplanned revascularization
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 19.0% with FFR-guided complete revascularization versus 20.4% with culprit-only PCI (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% CI 0.74–1.17; P=0.53), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes from randomization through 90 days of follow-up.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 4.8% of the CSL112 group and 5.2% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% CI 0.81–1.05; P=0.24), so CSL112 did not demonstrate significant superiority over placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Any or severe medically assessed RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease in infants through 6 months of age, and infant safety through 12 months of age.
brief_rationale: The abstract identifies multiple primary outcomes. Both RSV disease outcomes favored vaccination, but enrollment stopped because of increased preterm birth, and the abstract does not specify an overall success rule combining efficacy and infant safety outcomes.

primary_endpoint_description: Biochemical response at month 12, defined as an alkaline phosphatase level below 1.67 times the upper limit of normal with a decrease of at least 15% from baseline and a normal total bilirubin level.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred more often with seladelpar than placebo (61.7% vs. 20.0%; difference 41.7 percentage points, 95% CI 27.7 to 53.4; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Number of new gadolinium-enhancing T1-weighted MRI lesions at week 12 relative to week 8
brief_rationale: Both frexalimab regimens reduced the primary endpoint versus pooled placebo: rate ratio 0.11 (95% CI, 0.03–0.38) for 1200 mg intravenously and 0.21 (95% CI, 0.08–0.56) for 300 mg subcutaneously. Both confidence intervals excluded 1 in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: At week 52: (1) NASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis and (2) fibrosis improvement by at least one stage with no worsening of the NAFLD activity score.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored each resmetirom dose over placebo and were statistically significant (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The abstract concludes that both doses were superior to placebo for both endpoints.

primary_endpoint_description: Total score on the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) after 12 weeks of treatment
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored NALL over placebo: mean SARA change was -1.97 versus -0.60, with a least-squares mean difference of -1.28 points (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.65; P<0.001). Because lower scores indicate better neurologic status, this met the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Surgical-site infection, comprising superficial incisional infection within 30 days or deep incisional or organ-space infection within 90 days, analyzed separately in open- and closed-fracture populations.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome favored iodine and was statistically significant in the closed-fracture population (P=0.049) but not in the open-fracture population (P=0.45). The abstract does not specify an overall success rule for these separate primary analyses.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death or moderate or severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks of postmenstrual age
brief_rationale: The primary-outcome event occurred in 69.2% of the ibuprofen group versus 63.5% of the placebo group (adjusted risk ratio 1.09, 95% CI 0.98–1.20; P=0.10). Ibuprofen did not produce the intended significant reduction versus placebo, so the superiority endpoint was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Four-step primary hierarchical outcome comprising all-cause death, cardiovascular-related hospitalization, change from baseline in NT-proBNP level, and change from baseline in 6-minute walk distance.
brief_rationale: The prespecified primary hierarchical analysis significantly favored acoramidis over placebo (P<0.001), with a win ratio of 1.8 (95% CI, 1.4 to 2.2), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: New stroke within 90 days (primary efficacy outcome) and moderate-to-severe bleeding within 90 days (primary safety outcome).
brief_rationale: New stroke was significantly reduced with clopidogrel plus aspirin (7.3% vs 9.2%; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66–0.94; P=0.008), but moderate-to-severe bleeding was significantly increased (0.9% vs 0.4%; HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.07–4.04; P=0.03). Both are explicitly designated primary outcomes, and no overall success rule for these mixed results is stated.

primary_endpoint_description: Any incident infection with Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, or Treponema pallidum during follow-up.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint incidence was not significantly lower with doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis than with standard care (relative risk 0.88, 95% CI 0.60–1.29; P=0.51), so the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: PCR-confirmed influenza (A or B) among adults 50 to 64 years of age, the primary age group
brief_rationale: In the primary age group, PCR-confirmed influenza occurred less often with recombinant vaccine than with standard-dose vaccine, with relative vaccine effectiveness of 15.3% (95% CI, 5.9% to 23.8%; P=0.002), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Biochemical response at week 52, defined as alkaline phosphatase below 1.67 times the upper limit of normal with at least a 15% reduction from baseline and normal total bilirubin.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred in 51% of elafibranor-treated patients versus 4% receiving placebo, a favorable difference of 47 percentage points (95% CI, 32 to 57; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Improvement of at least 2 points on the patient-rated Clinical Global Impression of Change scale at week 18 (6 weeks after the second injection).
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 31% of patients receiving botulinum toxin versus 9% receiving placebo (relative risk 3.37, 95% CI 1.35–8.42; P=0.009), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the log-transformed 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at month 12.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint showed a significantly greater reduction in proteinuria with sibeprenlimab than with placebo, meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Effective response, defined as at least a 50% reduction in bleeding episodes during the year after treatment versus the year before treatment.
brief_rationale: Effective response occurred in 68.6% of the 100-mg group and 51.0% of the 50-mg group versus 16.0% with placebo, with a significant simultaneous comparison across groups (P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy: freedom at 1 year from above-ankle target-limb amputation, target-vessel occlusion, clinically driven target-lesion revascularization, and binary target-lesion restenosis. Primary safety: freedom from major adverse limb events at 6 months and perioperative death.
brief_rationale: Both primary endpoints met their stated criteria. The scaffold was superior for the primary efficacy endpoint (74% vs. 44%; one-sided P<0.001) and met noninferiority for the primary safety endpoint (one-sided P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Respiratory and cardiovascular organ support-free days through day 21, assessed on an ordinal scale combining in-hospital death and days free of organ support among survivors.
brief_rationale: The primary analysis yielded a 95.9% posterior probability of superiority, below the prespecified >99% threshold; therefore, the primary endpoint did not meet the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Two primary composite endpoints at 5 years: (1) death, stroke, or valve-, procedure-, or heart-failure–related rehospitalization; and (2) a hierarchical composite of death, disabling stroke, nondisabling stroke, and rehospitalization days assessed by win ratio.
brief_rationale: Neither primary endpoint showed significant superiority of TAVR over surgery: the first composite had P=0.07 and the hierarchical composite had a win ratio of 1.17 (95% CI, 0.90–1.51; P=0.25).

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in the protocol-specified interim efficacy analysis
brief_rationale: Selpercatinib significantly improved the explicitly identified primary endpoint versus physician's choice of cabozantinib or vandetanib (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.16–0.48; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review according to RECIST version 1.1.
brief_rationale: Both sotorasib–panitumumab dose groups had significantly longer progression-free survival than standard care, with hazard ratios of 0.49 (P=0.006) and 0.58 (P=0.03), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Metastasis-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review, comparing enzalutamide plus leuprolide with leuprolide alone.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint met the superiority criterion: enzalutamide plus leuprolide significantly improved metastasis-free survival versus leuprolide alone (hazard ratio for metastasis or death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.30–0.61; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Death from any cause during the 12 months after randomization
brief_rationale: Mortality was 44.1% with dexamethasone versus 49.0% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.85, 95% CI 0.66–1.10; P=0.22), so dexamethasone did not demonstrate significant superiority for the primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Remission at week 8, defined as a Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale score of 10 or less.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored esketamine over quetiapine: remission occurred in 27.1% versus 17.6% of patients (P=0.003), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Major adverse cardiac events at a median follow-up of 2 years, a composite of cardiac death, target-lesion myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-lesion revascularization.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred less often with OCT-guided PCI than with angiography-guided PCI (10.1% vs 14.1%; hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.50–0.98; P=0.035), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Dual primary end points: change from baseline to 52 weeks in the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire clinical summary score (KCCQ-CSS) and change in body weight.
brief_rationale: Both dual primary endpoints significantly favored semaglutide over placebo: KCCQ-CSS improved by an estimated 7.8 points more (95% CI, 4.8 to 10.9; P<0.001), and body weight decreased by an estimated 10.7 percentage points more (95% CI, -11.9 to -9.4; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiovascular death, stroke, or systemic embolism in a time-to-event analysis
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy outcome was less frequent with edoxaban than placebo, but the difference did not meet the superiority criterion (hazard ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.60–1.08; P=0.15).

primary_endpoint_description: Occurrence of a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, hospitalization for unstable angina, stroke, transient ischemic attack, peripheral arterial ischemia, revascularization, or death from an undetermined cause.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less often with pitavastatin than placebo (4.81 vs 7.32 per 1000 person-years; hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.48–0.90; P=0.002), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC) score over 240 weeks.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint showed a mean change of -1.43 with solanezumab versus -1.13 with placebo (difference, -0.30; 95% CI, -0.82 to 0.22; P=0.26), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Pathological complete response, defined as 0% viable tumor in the resected lung and lymph nodes.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 37% of the nivolumab-plus-chemotherapy group versus 7% of the chemotherapy-alone group (relative risk 5.34, 95% CI 1.34–21.23; P=0.02), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical remission at week 12 in the induction trial and at week 40 of the maintenance trial (52 weeks overall).
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored mirikizumab over placebo and were statistically significant: 24.2% versus 13.3% at induction week 12 and 49.9% versus 25.1% at maintenance week 40 (P<0.001 for both).

primary_endpoint_description: Two primary endpoints at 24 weeks: fibrosis improvement by at least one stage without worsening of NASH, and NASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis.
brief_rationale: Compared with placebo, the 30-mg and 44-mg pegozafermin groups had significant favorable results for fibrosis improvement (P=0.009 and P=0.008), and their between-group confidence intervals for NASH resolution also excluded no difference. Thus, both primary endpoints showed favorable superiority for these doses.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage change from baseline in body weight at week 26.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint is explicitly identified and descriptively favored orforglipron (-8.6% to -12.6%) over placebo (-2.0%) at week 26, but the abstract provides no statistical comparison, confidence interval, or stated success criterion sufficient to confirm that superiority was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Combined response at week 48 consisting of an undetectable HDV RNA level or a decrease of at least 2 log10 IU/mL from baseline, together with normalization of ALT.
brief_rationale: The primary-endpoint response occurred in 45% and 48% of patients receiving bulevirtide 2 mg and 10 mg, respectively, versus 2% in the control group; each dose comparison with control was statistically significant (P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Plasma HIV-1 RNA level of at least 50 copies per milliliter at week 48, assessed using the FDA snapshot algorithm.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 5.0% of the dolutegravir group and 5.1% of the ritonavir-boosted PI group (difference, -0.04 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.1 to 3.0). The abstract explicitly states that this met the prespecified 4-percentage-point noninferiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Survival with a favorable functional outcome at 6 months after injury, defined as a Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score of 5 or higher.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 53.7% of the tranexamic acid group and 53.5% of the placebo group (risk ratio 1.00, 95% CI 0.90–1.12; P=0.95), so tranexamic acid did not demonstrate favorable superiority over placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized rate of moderate or severe COPD exacerbations
brief_rationale: Dupilumab significantly reduced the explicitly identified primary endpoint versus placebo (0.78 vs 1.10 exacerbations annually; rate ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.58–0.86; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Excellent functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 or 1 at 90 days.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint occurred in 29.1% of the tirofiban group versus 22.2% of the aspirin group, favoring tirofiban (adjusted risk ratio 1.26, 95% CI 1.04–1.53; P=0.02), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Catheter-related bleeding of grade 2 to 4 after ultrasound-guided central venous catheter placement
brief_rationale: The relative risk for grade 2 to 4 bleeding with no transfusion versus prophylactic transfusion was 2.45 (90% CI, 1.27 to 4.70). Because the upper confidence bound exceeded the prespecified noninferiority margin of 3.5, withholding transfusion did not meet the noninferiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of severe postpartum hemorrhage (blood loss ≥1000 ml), laparotomy for bleeding, or maternal death from bleeding
brief_rationale: The primary-outcome event rate was significantly lower with the intervention than with usual care (1.6% vs. 4.3%; risk ratio 0.40, 95% CI 0.32–0.50; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Vaccine efficacy against seasonal RSV-associated lower respiratory tract illness with at least two signs or symptoms and with at least three signs or symptoms.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored RSVpreF: efficacy was 66.7% (96.66% CI, 28.8% to 85.8%) for illness with at least two symptoms and 85.7% (96.66% CI, 32.0% to 98.7%) for illness with at least three symptoms; both confidence intervals excluded no efficacy.

primary_endpoint_description: Death from prostate cancer at a median follow-up of 15 years
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was prostate cancer–specific death. Mortality was 3.1% with active monitoring, 2.2% with prostatectomy, and 2.9% with radiotherapy, with no significant overall difference (P=0.53); therefore, favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline at week 24 in 6-minute walk distance
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored sotatercept: the between-group difference in change in 6-minute walk distance was 40.8 m (95% CI, 27.5 to 54.1; P<0.001), demonstrating statistically significant superiority over placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel-related myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target-vessel revascularization.
brief_rationale: The primary composite endpoint occurred less often with intravascular imaging-guided PCI than with angiography-guided PCI (7.7% vs. 12.3%; hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.45–0.89; P=0.008), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Median duration of imaging-based progression-free survival according to independent review.
brief_rationale: Rucaparib significantly prolonged the explicitly identified primary outcome versus physician's choice, including in the BRCA subgroup (11.2 vs 6.4 months; HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.36–0.69; P<0.001) and intention-to-treat population (10.2 vs 6.4 months; HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.47–0.80; P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of Covid-19–related hospitalization (or transfer to a tertiary hospital) or an emergency department visit with observation for more than 6 hours within 28 days after randomization.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 2.7% of the interferon group versus 5.6% of the placebo group (relative risk 0.49; 95% Bayesian credible interval 0.30–0.76), with a posterior probability of superiority greater than 99.9%, meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Death from any cause at 90 days
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 0.78% of the aspirin group and 0.73% of the low-molecular-weight-heparin group. The between-group difference was 0.05 percentage points (96.2% CI, -0.27 to 0.38), satisfying the prespecified noninferiority margin of 0.75 percentage points (P<0.001 for noninferiority).

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure resulting in hospitalization, urgent coronary revascularization for unstable angina, and non-cancer-related death
brief_rationale: The primary composite outcome occurred in 10.4% with chlorthalidone versus 10.0% with hydrochlorothiazide (hazard ratio 1.04, 95% CI 0.94–1.16; P=0.45), so chlorthalidone did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in the total MDS-UPDRS score from baseline to 36 weeks
brief_rationale: The primary outcome worsened by 15.6 points with deferiprone versus 6.3 points with placebo, a significant difference of 9.3 points (95% CI, 6.3 to 12.2; P<0.001) in the unfavorable direction. Thus, deferiprone did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 12 in each baxdrostat dose group compared with placebo.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored baxdrostat: versus placebo, systolic blood pressure decreased by an additional 11.0 mm Hg with 2 mg (95% CI, -16.4 to -5.5; P<0.001) and 8.1 mm Hg with 1 mg (95% CI, -13.5 to -2.8; P=0.003), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, coronary revascularization, or death from cardiovascular causes
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 572 pemafibrate recipients and 560 placebo recipients (hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.91–1.15). Pemafibrate did not reduce cardiovascular events versus placebo, so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of progression of kidney disease or death from cardiovascular causes
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite outcome occurred less often with empagliflozin than placebo (13.1% vs 16.9%; hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.64–0.82; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage change in BMI from baseline to week 68
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored semaglutide: mean BMI changed by -16.1% versus +0.6% with placebo, for an estimated difference of -16.7 percentage points (95% CI, -20.3 to -13.2; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Good functional status at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin scale score of 0 to 3.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred in 46% of the thrombectomy group versus 23% of the control group (adjusted rate ratio 2.06, 95% CI 1.46–2.91; P<0.001), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Response at week 16, defined as a Total Improvement Score of at least 20 with no confirmed deterioration through week 16.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 79% of the IVIG group versus 44% of the placebo group, a favorable difference of 35 percentage points (95% CI, 17 to 53; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Glycated hemoglobin level at 24 weeks
brief_rationale: The intervention produced a significantly lower 24-week glycated hemoglobin level than usual care (adjusted mean between-group difference, -0.5 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.7 to -0.3; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Development of moderately severe or severe pancreatitis during hospitalization
brief_rationale: The primary outcome did not differ significantly between aggressive and moderate fluid resuscitation (22.1% vs 17.3%; adjusted relative risk 1.30, 95% CI 0.78–2.18; P=0.32), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Birth of an infant who was large for gestational age, defined as birth weight above the 90th percentile according to Fenton–World Health Organization standards.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 8.8% with lower glycemic criteria versus 8.9% with higher criteria (adjusted relative risk 0.98, 95% CI 0.80–1.19; P=0.82). Thus, lower criteria did not produce a statistically significant favorable reduction in large-for-gestational-age births.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the total number of active joints (sum of swollen and tender joints) at week 24
brief_rationale: The revised primary endpoint favored litifilimab: least-squares mean change was -15.0 versus -11.6 with placebo, for a mean difference of -3.4 joints (95% CI, -6.7 to -0.2; P=0.04), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of an unfavorable outcome, defined as treatment failure or clinical or bacteriologic disease relapse at 26 weeks after treatment completion, in the modified intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint is explicit and outcomes were reported across the four regimens, but the abstract provides no prespecified superiority, noninferiority, equivalence, or threshold-based success criterion. Therefore, whether the primary endpoint met the trial's success criterion cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death, myocardial infarction, or revascularization at 24 months after randomization
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 8.1% with FFR guidance and 8.5% with IVUS guidance. The upper bound of the one-sided 97.5% confidence interval for the absolute difference was 2.2 percentage points, below the prespecified 2.5-point noninferiority margin (P=0.01 for noninferiority), so noninferiority was met.

primary_endpoint_description: ACR20 response at week 12, with each olokizumab dose tested for superiority to placebo.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was met: ACR20 response rates were 70.3% and 71.4% with olokizumab every 2 and 4 weeks, respectively, versus 44.4% with placebo; both superiority comparisons were favorable and significant (P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized relapse rate in each of the ULTIMATE I and ULTIMATE II trials.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored ublituximab in both trials: annualized relapse rates were 0.08 versus 0.19 in ULTIMATE I (rate ratio 0.41; P<0.001) and 0.09 versus 0.18 in ULTIMATE II (rate ratio 0.51; P=0.002), demonstrating significant superiority over teriflunomide.

primary_endpoint_description: Incident total, nonvertebral, and hip fractures
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoints all failed to show favorable superiority of vitamin D3 over placebo: total fractures HR 0.98 (P=0.70), nonvertebral fractures HR 0.97 (P=0.50), and hip fractures HR 1.01 (P=0.96).

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline to week 52 in the sum of MDS-UPDRS parts I, II, and III scores.
brief_rationale: Neither prasinezumab dose showed favorable superiority over placebo on the explicitly identified primary endpoint (1500 mg: difference −2.0, P=0.24; 4500 mg: difference −0.6, P=0.72).

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival and overall survival in the PD-L1 CPS-10 subgroup, CPS-1 subgroup, and intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Overall survival met the significance criterion in the CPS-10 subgroup but was not significant in the CPS-1 subgroup and was not tested in the intention-to-treat population; progression-free survival was reported previously. Because multiple primary endpoints/populations had mixed or incompletely reported results and no overall success rule is stated, overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean change in visual acuity over the 2-year trial period
brief_rationale: The primary outcome showed mean improvements of 15.0 letters with aflibercept monotherapy and 14.0 letters with bevacizumab-first treatment; the adjusted difference was 0.8 letters (95% CI, -0.9 to 2.5; P=0.37), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Modified progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies modified progression-free survival as the primary endpoint but states only that it was reported previously. This follow-up report provides overall survival as a key secondary endpoint and does not adequately report the primary endpoint result.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death or neurodevelopmental impairment at 22 to 36 months of age
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 52.5% of the erythropoietin group and 49.5% of the placebo group (relative risk 1.03, 95% CI 0.86–1.24; P=0.74). Erythropoietin did not produce the intended favorable reduction versus placebo, so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored ibrutinib: median progression-free survival was 80.6 versus 52.9 months (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.59–0.96; P=0.01), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Prevention of symptomatic Covid-19 beginning at least 7 days after the second injection
brief_rationale: The explicitly stated primary objective was vaccine efficacy against symptomatic Covid-19. Efficacy was 69.5% (95% CI, 56.7% to 78.8%), a favorable result with the confidence interval excluding no efficacy.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy endpoint: RT-PCR-confirmed symptomatic Covid-19 through day 183; primary safety endpoint: incidence of adverse events after a single dose.
brief_rationale: Symptomatic Covid-19 occurred in 0.2% with AZD7442 versus 1.0% with placebo, a favorable 76.7% relative risk reduction (95% CI, 46.0%–90.0%; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion. Adverse-event incidence was similar between groups (35.3% versus 34.2%), with no evident safety concern.

The abstract reports recurrence-free percentages through day 168 and between-group comparisons, but it does not explicitly identify any endpoint as the prespecified primary endpoint. Therefore, primary-endpoint success cannot be assessed under the stated criteria.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy outcome: survival without moderate or severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks postmenstrual age; primary safety outcome: survival without moderate or severe neurodevelopmental impairment at 22–26 months corrected age.
brief_rationale: Neither explicitly identified primary outcome showed favorable superiority with hydrocortisone. Survival without bronchopulmonary dysplasia had an adjusted rate ratio of 1.27 (95% CI, 0.93–1.74), and survival without neurodevelopmental impairment had an adjusted rate ratio of 0.98 (95% CI, 0.81–1.18); both confidence intervals included 1.

primary_endpoint_description: Medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection through 150 days after injection
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint occurred in 1.2% of nirsevimab recipients versus 5.0% of placebo recipients, corresponding to 74.5% efficacy (95% CI, 49.6–87.1; P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Vaccine efficacy against moderate to severe-critical Covid-19 with onset at least 14 days and at least 28 days after administration in the per-protocol population.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoints favored Ad26.COV2.S: efficacy was 56.3% at ≥14 days (95% CI, 51.3–60.8) and 52.9% at ≥28 days (95% CI, 47.1–58.1), with both confidence intervals excluding no efficacy.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary safety endpoints of adjudicated major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cancers excluding nonmelanoma skin cancer, comparing combined tofacitinib doses with a TNF inhibitor.
brief_rationale: Noninferiority required the upper bound of each two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio to be below 1.8. The upper bounds were 1.94 for MACE and 2.09 for cancers, and the abstract explicitly states that noninferiority was not shown.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrence of Clostridioides difficile infection through 8 weeks after treatment
brief_rationale: The explicitly stated primary efficacy objective was superiority of SER-109 over placebo in reducing recurrence through 8 weeks. Recurrence was 12% with SER-109 versus 40% with placebo (relative risk 0.32, 95% CI 0.18–0.58; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Event-free survival according to blinded central review
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored axi-cel over standard care: median event-free survival was 8.3 versus 2.0 months (hazard ratio for event or death, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.31–0.51; P<0.001), and the abstract states that superiority was demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: PGA response at week 12, defined as a Physician's Global Assessment score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) with a decrease from baseline of at least 2 points.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored tapinarof in both phase 3 trials: PGA response rates were 35.4% versus 6.0% in trial 1 and 40.2% versus 6.3% in trial 2, with P<0.001 for both comparisons, meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. Cytoreductive surgery plus chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival versus chemotherapy alone (median 53.7 vs 46.0 months; hazard ratio for death 0.75, 95% CI 0.59–0.96; P=0.02), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Venous thromboembolism, a composite of asymptomatic deep-vein thrombosis, confirmed symptomatic venous thromboembolism, or death from any cause.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy outcome met the stated criteria: twice-daily milvexian showed a significant dose-response relationship (one-sided P<0.001), and its 12% venous thromboembolism incidence was significantly below the prespecified 30% benchmark (one-sided P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Echocardiographic progression of latent rheumatic heart disease at 2 years
brief_rationale: Progression occurred in 0.8% of the prophylaxis group versus 8.2% of controls (risk difference, -7.5 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.2 to -4.7; P<0.001), demonstrating significant benefit on the explicitly identified primary outcome.

The abstract reports that the immunogenicity bridging measure met a prespecified success criterion, but it does not explicitly identify this or any other measure as the trial's primary endpoint or primary outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to the first asthma worsening
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored placebo rather than risankizumab: median time to first asthma worsening was 40 versus 86 days (hazard ratio 1.46, 95% CI 1.05–2.04; P=0.03). Thus, risankizumab did not achieve favorable superiority and instead worsened the primary outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of stroke, acute coronary syndrome, acute decompensated heart failure, coronary revascularization, atrial fibrillation, or death from cardiovascular causes.
brief_rationale: The primary composite outcome occurred less often with intensive treatment than with standard treatment (3.5% vs 4.6%; hazard ratio 0.74, 95% CI 0.60–0.92; P=0.007), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to the composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite outcome occurred less often with finerenone than placebo (12.4% vs 14.2%; hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.76–0.98; P=0.03), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of in-hospital all-cause death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, cardiac transplant or mechanical circulatory support, nonfatal myocardial infarction, neurologist-diagnosed transient ischemic attack or stroke, or initiation of renal replacement therapy.
brief_rationale: The primary composite occurred in 49% of the milrinone group and 54% of the dobutamine group, with no significant between-group difference (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.69-1.19; P=0.47); thus, favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Development of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection through day 28 among participants without baseline SARS-CoV-2 infection or previous immunity (seronegative).
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 11 of 753 participants (1.5%) receiving REGEN-COV versus 59 of 752 (7.8%) receiving placebo, a favorable relative risk reduction of 81.4% with P<0.001, meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall response (complete or partial response) at week 24
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored ruxolitinib over control (49.7% vs. 25.6%; odds ratio 2.99; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Hematologic complete response
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred significantly more often with daratumumab than with control (53.3% vs. 18.1%; relative risk ratio 2.9, 95% CI 2.1–4.1; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Attenuation of gluten-induced mucosal damage, measured by the change in the ratio of villus height to crypt depth.
brief_rationale: All three ZED1227 doses showed favorable differences versus placebo in the primary endpoint, with 95% confidence intervals excluding no difference and P values of 0.001 or less, meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in glycated hemoglobin level from baseline to 40 weeks.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies change in glycated hemoglobin at 40 weeks as the primary endpoint and states that all tirzepatide doses were noninferior, and subsequently superior, to semaglutide for this endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Negative nucleic acid amplification test for rectal chlamydia (microbiologic cure) at 4 weeks
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored doxycycline: microbiologic cure was 96.9% with doxycycline versus 76.4% with azithromycin, with an adjusted risk difference of 19.9 percentage points (95% CI, 14.6 to 25.3; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Death from any cause at 6 months
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 50% of the hypothermia group versus 48% of the normothermia group (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.94–1.14; P=0.37). Hypothermia did not demonstrate favorable superiority in reducing 6-month mortality.

primary_endpoint_description: Infant survival to discharge from the neonatal intensive care unit
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored FETO: survival to discharge was 40% versus 15% with expectant care (relative risk 2.67, 95% CI 1.22–6.11; P=0.009). The group-sequential superiority trial was stopped early for efficacy, indicating that the prespecified success criterion was met.
The abstract reports safety and immunogenicity outcomes but does not explicitly identify any endpoint as the prespecified primary endpoint; therefore, primary-endpoint success cannot be assessed.

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized rate of asthma exacerbations over 52 weeks
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored tezepelumab: annualized exacerbation rates were 0.93 versus 2.10 with placebo (rate ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.37–0.53; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary end points of safety and vaccine efficacy against laboratory-confirmed symptomatic Covid-19 occurring at least 7 days after dose 2 among participants without previous SARS-CoV-2 infection.
brief_rationale: The efficacy primary endpoint favored vaccine (49.4% efficacy; 95% CI, 6.1% to 72.8%), and safety findings were summarized as rare serious adverse events with greater reactogenicity. However, no prespecified safety criterion or overall success rule for the co-primary safety and efficacy endpoints is reported.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in body weight from randomization to the end of the 1-year treatment period in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: All three active-treatment strategies produced significantly greater weight loss than placebo on the explicitly identified primary endpoint, with favorable 95% confidence intervals and P values (exercise P=0.03; liraglutide and combination P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Primary cardiovascular safety endpoint: time to first MACE (all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke), pooled across both trials; primary efficacy endpoint: mean change in hemoglobin from baseline during weeks 24–36 in each trial.
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy endpoint met its prespecified noninferiority margin in both trials, whereas the pooled primary safety endpoint did not meet its noninferiority margin. No overall success rule for these mixed primary results is stated.
The abstract reports overall HIV-1 acquisition and prespecified analyses by isolate sensitivity, but it does not explicitly identify any endpoint as the primary endpoint or an unambiguous equivalent.

primary_endpoint_description: Diagnosis of gestational diabetes; large-for-gestational-age infants; a perinatal composite of stillbirth, neonatal death, shoulder dystocia, fracture, or birth-related nerve palsy; gestational hypertension or preeclampsia; and primary cesarean section.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies five primary outcomes. Gestational diabetes diagnoses differed significantly between groups, whereas the four maternal and perinatal complication outcomes did not. Because no overall success rule for these multiple primary outcomes is stated, overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage of participants achieving menstrual blood-loss response (<80 mL and ≥50% reduction from baseline) with relugolix combination therapy versus placebo in each trial
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored relugolix combination therapy in both replicate trials: 73% versus 19% in L1 and 71% versus 15% in L2, with P<0.001 for both placebo comparisons.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage of patients with complete (100%) reduction in the number of lesions in the application area at day 57
brief_rationale: In both trials, complete clearance at day 57 was significantly more frequent with tirbanibulin than with vehicle: 44% vs 5% in trial 1 and 54% vs 13% in trial 2, with P<0.001 for both comparisons. Thus, the primary superiority endpoint was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Death within 90 days
brief_rationale: The lower-oxygenation target did not reduce 90-day mortality versus the higher target (42.9% vs 42.4%; adjusted risk ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.94–1.11; P=0.64), so the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Prevention of Covid-19 illness beginning at least 14 days after the second injection among participants without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection
brief_rationale: The vaccine significantly reduced primary-endpoint Covid-19 cases versus placebo (11 vs 185), with 94.1% efficacy (95% CI, 89.3%–96.8%; P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy: between-group difference in change from baseline to 4 months in off-medication MDS-UPDRS part III motor score for the more affected body side; primary safety: procedure-related complications at 4 months.
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy outcome significantly favored focused ultrasound (between-group difference 8.1 points, 95% CI 6.0–10.3; P<0.001), but the abstract also identifies a primary safety outcome and gives no overall success rule or prespecified safety criterion. Overall primary-endpoint success is therefore indeterminable.

The abstract identifies two measures only as “key end points” and does not explicitly designate either as the primary or prespecified primary endpoint. Therefore, primary-endpoint success cannot be assessed.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to kidney failure, a sustained decrease of at least 40% in eGFR from baseline, or death from renal causes
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite outcome occurred less often with finerenone than placebo (17.8% vs 21.1%; hazard ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.73–0.93; P=0.001), demonstrating statistically significant favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: In-hospital mortality in four pairwise comparisons of remdesivir, hydroxychloroquine, lopinavir, and interferon beta-1a versus their respective controls.
brief_rationale: The primary mortality analyses showed no significant favorable reduction for any regimen: all 95% confidence intervals for the death rate ratios included 1 and all P values exceeded 0.05.

primary_endpoint_description: Rate of fractures per 100 person-years over 18 months
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was the fracture rate over 18 months. Neither targeted exercise nor multifactorial fall prevention reduced fractures versus advice by mail; rate ratios were 1.20 (95% CI, 0.91–1.59) and 1.30 (95% CI, 0.99–1.71), respectively. Thus, favorable superiority was not achieved.

primary_endpoint_description: Endogenous insulin production assessed by the 4-hour C-peptide area under the concentration-time curve during a mixed-meal tolerance test at week 52.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was significantly higher with golimumab than placebo at week 52 (mean 4-hour C-peptide AUC 0.64 vs 0.43 pmol/mL; P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol level at week 16 with evinacumab compared with placebo.
brief_rationale: Evinacumab produced favorable placebo-adjusted LDL cholesterol reductions at week 16, including reductions of 38.5 to 56.0 percentage points for subcutaneous regimens (P<0.001 for each) and 50.5 percentage points for intravenous 15 mg/kg (P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Resolution of NASH with no worsening of fibrosis in patients with stage F2 or F3 fibrosis
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred in 59% of patients receiving semaglutide 0.4 mg versus 17% receiving placebo, a statistically significant favorable difference (P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in SARS-CoV-2 viral load at day 11
brief_rationale: The 2800-mg LY-CoV555 dose produced a significantly greater reduction in viral load than placebo on the explicitly identified primary outcome (difference, -0.53 log units; 95% CI, -0.98 to -0.08; P=0.02), meeting a favorable superiority criterion, although the other two doses did not.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in gastrointestinal eosinophil count from baseline to 2 weeks after the final dose, comparing placebo with the combined AK002 group
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored AK002: mean eosinophil count changed by -86% with combined AK002 versus 9% with placebo, with a least-squares mean difference of -98 percentage points (95% CI, -121 to -76; P<0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in DAS28-CRP at week 12, assessed for noninferiority of upadacitinib versus abatacept.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored upadacitinib (between-group difference, -0.52 points; 95% CI, -0.69 to -0.35), and the reported noninferiority criterion was met (P<0.001 for noninferiority).

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival in the overall randomized population and in the PD-L1-positive population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival in both populations. Maintenance avelumab significantly prolonged overall survival versus control in the overall population (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.56–0.86; P=0.001) and the PD-L1-positive population (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40–0.79; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to disease progression, defined as a composite of major surgery, endoscopic excision of advanced adenomas, diagnosis of high-grade dysplasia in the rectum or pouch, or progression of duodenal disease.
brief_rationale: The combination did not significantly reduce disease progression versus either monotherapy: HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.39–1.32; P=0.29) versus sulindac and HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.36–1.24) versus eflornithine. Thus, the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to tracheostomy decannulation
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was time to decannulation. It was shorter with the suctioning-frequency strategy than with capping (median 6 vs 13 days; absolute difference 7 days, 95% CI 5 to 9), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Relapse-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was relapse-free survival. At 5 years, relapse-free survival favored dabrafenib plus trametinib over placebo (52% vs 36%; hazard ratio for relapse or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.42–0.61), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Percent change in LDL cholesterol level from baseline to week 24
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored evolocumab: mean LDL cholesterol changed by -44.5% with evolocumab versus -6.2% with placebo, a difference of -38.3 percentage points (P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrence of cellulitis
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was cellulitis recurrence. Recurrence was significantly lower with compression therapy than with education alone (15% vs 40%; hazard ratio 0.23, 95% CI 0.09–0.59; P=0.002), and the trial was stopped for efficacy.

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized relapse rate
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored ofatumumab in both trials: annualized relapse rates were 0.11 versus 0.22 in trial 1 and 0.10 versus 0.25 in trial 2, with P<0.001 for both comparisons, meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical status at 15 days assessed on a seven-level ordinal scale in the modified intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Neither hydroxychloroquine alone nor hydroxychloroquine plus azithromycin significantly improved the explicitly identified primary outcome versus standard care (OR 1.21, 95% CI 0.69–2.11, P=1.00; and OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.57–1.73, P=1.00, respectively).

primary_endpoint_description: 28-day mortality
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Mortality was significantly lower with dexamethasone than with usual care overall (22.9% vs 25.7%; age-adjusted rate ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.75–0.93; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Death from any cause at 90 days
brief_rationale: The accelerated strategy did not reduce the primary outcome versus the standard strategy: 90-day mortality was 43.9% versus 43.7% (relative risk 1.00, 95% CI 0.93–1.09; P=0.92), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: First adjudicated serious fall injury, assessed in a time-to-first-event analysis
brief_rationale: The primary outcome did not differ significantly in the favorable direction between the intervention and control groups (hazard ratio 0.92, 95% CI 0.80–1.06; P=0.25), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Achievement after 24 months of a hemoglobin level of at least 9.0 g/dL or a fetal hemoglobin level of at least 20%.
brief_rationale: The primary-outcome thresholds were reached by 86% of children receiving dose-escalated hydroxyurea versus 37% receiving fixed-dose hydroxyurea (P<0.001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Annual rate of moderate or severe COPD exacerbations in the modified intention-to-treat population using on-treatment data
brief_rationale: Both budesonide-dose triple therapies significantly reduced the primary endpoint versus each dual therapy comparator, with rate ratios of 0.75–0.87 and P values of 0.003 or lower, demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Annualized rate of composite porphyria attacks among patients with acute intermittent porphyria over 6 months
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored givosiran: mean annualized attack rates were 3.2 with givosiran versus 12.5 with placebo, a 74% lower rate (P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage of women with recurrence of bacterial vaginosis by week 12
brief_rationale: Recurrence by week 12 was significantly lower with Lactin-V than placebo (30% vs 45%; risk ratio 0.66, 95% CI 0.44–0.87; P=0.01), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score at week 4
brief_rationale: SEP-363856 produced a significantly greater favorable reduction in PANSS total score than placebo at week 4 (least-squares mean difference, -7.5 points; 95% CI, -11.9 to -3.0; P=0.001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Total Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) score at 1 year
brief_rationale: At 1 year, mean WOMAC scores were lower (better) with physical therapy than with glucocorticoid injection (37.0 vs. 55.8), with a between-group difference of 18.8 points (95% CI, 5.0 to 32.6) favoring physical therapy; the confidence interval excluded no difference.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death from cardiovascular causes or first hospitalization for heart failure
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less often with vericiguat than placebo (35.5% vs 38.5%; hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.98; P=0.02), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol at day 510 and time-adjusted percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol between days 90 and 540.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored inclisiran over placebo, with between-group differences of -47.9 and -44.3 percentage points, respectively; both were statistically significant (P<0.001).

primary_endpoint_description: Leg-pain intensity on a 0-to-10 visual analogue scale at 6 months after enrollment
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored microdiskectomy: mean leg-pain intensity was 2.8 with surgery versus 5.2 with nonsurgical care (adjusted mean difference, 2.4; 95% CI, 1.4 to 3.4; P<0.001). The abstract concludes that microdiskectomy was superior for this endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Time from randomization to clinical improvement, defined as either a two-point improvement on a seven-category ordinal scale or hospital discharge, whichever occurred first.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint showed no significant favorable difference between lopinavir-ritonavir and standard care (hazard ratio 1.31, 95% CI 0.95–1.80); therefore, the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints in each trial: placebo-corrected percentage change in LDL cholesterol from baseline to day 510 and time-adjusted percentage change in LDL cholesterol from baseline after day 90 through day 540.
brief_rationale: In both ORION-10 and ORION-11, inclisiran produced favorable reductions of approximately 49% to 54% for both coprimary LDL-cholesterol endpoints, with P<0.001 for all comparisons versus placebo; thus, both coprimary superiority endpoints were met in both trials.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response at definitive surgery and event-free survival in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Pathological complete response significantly favored pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy (64.8% vs 51.2%; difference 13.6 percentage points; P<0.001). Event-free survival was also favorable (HR 0.63; 95% CI, 0.43–0.93), but the abstract does not report its prespecified inferential criterion or state the overall success rule for the two primary endpoints.

primary_endpoint_description: Percent change from baseline in the mean peak pruritus score on the numerical rating scale at week 4
brief_rationale: The primary outcome favored nemolizumab: mean peak pruritus decreased by 53.0% versus 20.2% with placebo, a difference of -32.8 percentage points (95% CI, -46.8 to -18.8; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Mortality at 90 days
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was 90-day mortality. Mortality was 42.4% with nonsedation versus 37.0% with light sedation (difference 5.4 percentage points, 95% CI -2.2 to 12.2; P=0.65), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Menstrual blood loss below 80 mL during the final treatment month and at least a 50% reduction from baseline to the final month
brief_rationale: In both placebo-controlled phase 3 trials, significantly more women receiving elagolix plus add-back therapy met the primary endpoint than women receiving placebo (68.5% vs 8.7% in UF-1 and 76.5% vs 10% in UF-2; P<0.001 for both), demonstrating favorable superiority.

The abstract explicitly identifies overall survival as a secondary endpoint and does not explicitly identify the trial's prespecified primary endpoint. Progression-free survival is mentioned but is not labeled as primary, so primary-endpoint success cannot be assessed.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy outcome: composite of death or thromboembolic events; primary safety outcome: major, disabling, or life-threatening bleeding.
brief_rationale: Rivaroxaban did not show favorable superiority on either primary outcome. Death or thromboembolic events were significantly more frequent with rivaroxaban (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.01–1.81; P=0.04), and major, disabling, or life-threatening bleeding was also numerically more frequent (HR 1.50, 95% CI 0.95–2.37; P=0.08).

primary_endpoint_description: Number of ventilator-free days from randomization through day 28
brief_rationale: The primary outcome did not differ significantly between conservative and usual oxygen therapy (median 21.3 vs 22.1 days; absolute difference, -0.3 days; 95% CI, -2.1 to 1.6; P=0.80), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Disease-free survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The carboplatin arm had significantly better disease-free survival than control (three-year estimates 92.3% vs 85.8%; hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.95; P=0.03), meeting the favorable superiority criterion despite violation of the proportional hazards assumption.

primary_endpoint_description: Live birth after the first embryo transfer and cumulative live birth within 12 months after randomisation (up to three transfer cycles).
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary outcomes failed to show superiority of PGT-A: live birth after first transfer was 48.4% versus 46.2% (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.76-1.58; P=0.64), and cumulative live birth was 60.4% versus 60.9% (OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.67-1.43; P=0.92).

primary_endpoint_description: Shoulder pain at rest and shoulder pain on arm activity at 10 years, both measured using a 0-100 visual analogue scale, in the primary ASD versus placebo surgery comparison.
brief_rationale: Neither primary outcome showed a favorable between-group benefit for ASD versus placebo surgery: mean differences were -1.5 points (95% CI -8.6 to 5.6) for pain at rest and -3.2 points (95% CI -13.0 to 6.5) for pain on arm activity, with no significant differences and effects below the 15-point minimally important difference.

primary_endpoint_description: Conversion to sinus rhythm within 30 minutes of completion of the drug infusion.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored vernakalant over procainamide (62.4% vs 48.3%; adjusted absolute difference 15.0%, 95% CI 4.6% to 25.0%; P=0.005), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall response rate at week 8, defined as at least two consecutive platelet counts ≥30×10^9/L, a minimum doubling from baseline, and no bleeding.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored CM313: overall response was 83% (25/30) with CM313 versus 20% (3/15) with placebo, a difference of 63.3% (95% CI 33.7% to 81.3%; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of grade ≥2 hand-foot syndrome occurring for the first time during capecitabine treatment in the intention-to-treat analysis.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred less often with methylcobalamin than placebo (14.5% vs 29.1%; risk difference −14.5%, 95% CI −24.9% to −4.1%; one-sided P=0.003), demonstrating statistically significant favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage of patients achieving at least a 4-point reduction from baseline to week 12 in weekly mean 24-hour worst itching intensity numerical rating scale (WI-NRS) score.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred in 37% of the anrikefon group versus 15% of the placebo group (P<0.001), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Self-reported PTSD symptoms measured by the PDS-5 at six months.
brief_rationale: The intervention produced a statistically significant favorable between-group difference of 4.7 PDS-5 points at six months, but this was below the predefined six-point minimal clinically important difference; therefore, the primary endpoint did not meet the stated success criterion.

This is a three-year extended follow-up report. Although three-year vein graft occlusion is listed under “main outcome measures,” the abstract does not explicitly identify it—or report the original trial endpoint—as the prespecified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of hypoxia (75% ≤ SpO2 <90% for <60 seconds) during the procedure
brief_rationale: HFNC significantly reduced the explicitly identified primary outcome from 21.2% with regular nasal cannula oxygenation to 2.0% (difference −19.14 percentage points, 95% CI −23.09 to −15.36; P<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of diabetes remission over 12 months, defined as HbA1c <6.5% and fasting plasma glucose <126 mg/dL without antidiabetic drugs for at least 2 months.
brief_rationale: Remission occurred in 44% with dapagliflozin plus calorie restriction versus 28% with placebo plus calorie restriction (risk ratio 1.56, 95% CI 1.17-2.09; P=0.002), and the abstract explicitly states that the predefined primary endpoint was met.

primary_endpoint_description: 28-day all-cause mortality after randomisation
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 23.4% of the thymosin α1 group versus 24.1% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.77-1.27; P=0.93), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Quality of shared decision making measured by OPTION12, knowledge of atrial fibrillation and its management, and decisional conflict
brief_rationale: Three primary outcomes are explicitly identified. Results were favorable and statistically significant for all three with the combined aids and the encounter aid alone, but the patient aid alone did not significantly improve decisional conflict. Because the abstract does not state the overall success rule for these multiple primary outcomes and intervention comparisons, overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Survival to hospital discharge
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge. Survival was 10.7% with intraosseous access versus 10.3% with intravenous access (odds ratio 1.04, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.42; P=0.81), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite adverse perinatal outcome
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 6% of each group (pessary 19/303 vs progesterone 17/309; RR 1.1, 95% CI 0.60-2.2). The prespecified favorable superiority of pessary was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Binary decision of whether the physician sat at any point during the patient encounter
