brief_rationale: For the explicitly identified primary outcome, chlorfenapyr-pyrethroid LLINs significantly reduced malaria incidence versus pyrethroid-only LLINs (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.42-0.70; p<0.0001), meeting a favorable superiority criterion. Pyriproxyfen-pyrethroid LLINs did not show superiority (p=0.28).

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival in all randomly assigned patients on an intention-to-treat basis
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. Adjuvant S-1 significantly improved overall survival versus observation (adjusted HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.51-0.94; one-sided p=0.0080), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Event-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was event-free survival. Three-year event-free survival was 67% with the US dose-intensive regimen versus 61% with the European regimen; the adjusted HR was 0.71 (95% credible interval 0.55–0.92), with greater than 0.99 probability that the true HR was below 1.0. The authors concluded that the US regimen was more effective.

primary_endpoint_description: Between-group difference in mean percentage change from baseline in the Vasomotor Symptom Severity Score for moderate and severe hot flushes and night sweats after 28 days of treatment.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored Q-122 over placebo: mean change was -39% versus -26%, with a statistically significant between-group difference (p=0.018), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in unattended office systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 4
brief_rationale: Both aprocitentan doses produced significantly greater reductions in office systolic blood pressure than placebo at week 4: differences of -3.8 mm Hg (p=0.0042) and -3.7 mm Hg (p=0.0046), with 97.5% confidence intervals excluding zero in the favorable direction. The stated superiority criterion was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Safety and tolerability of multiple weekly doses of LY3437943
brief_rationale: The primary outcome was explicitly identified as safety and tolerability. Although adverse events were reported and the interpretation describes an acceptable safety profile, the abstract provides no prespecified criterion or threshold defining primary-endpoint success.

primary_endpoint_description: Objectively confirmed venous thromboembolism in the intention-to-treat population; the primary safety outcome was major bleeding.
brief_rationale: Intermediate-dose heparin did not significantly reduce the primary efficacy outcome versus low-dose heparin (2% vs 3%; RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.32–1.47; p=0.33). Major bleeding was also similar (4% vs 4%; RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.65–2.09). Thus, favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of all-cause mortality or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) types 3-5 bleeding at 30 days
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was significantly reduced with bivalirudin versus heparin (3.06% vs 4.39%; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.53-0.91; p=0.0070), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrent hospital admissions for heart failure and cardiovascular death
brief_rationale: The primary outcome favored ferric derisomaltose but did not meet the conventional superiority criterion in the main analysis (rate ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.66–1.02; p=0.070). The significant prespecified COVID-19 sensitivity analysis does not change the negative primary analysis.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiovascular-related death or hospital admission with myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, or congestive heart failure during the 4-year trial period
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 21.4% with personalised cooler dialysate versus 22.4% with standard-temperature dialysate (adjusted HR 1.00, 96% CI 0.89–1.11; p=0.93), so the prespecified favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Depression symptom severity and alcohol use severity at 12 months, assessed separately in the HIV, diabetes, and pooled cohorts.
brief_rationale: The primary depression outcome favored both intervention approaches versus usual care, whereas the primary alcohol-use outcome showed no intervention effect. The abstract does not state an overall success rule for these multiple primary outcomes, so overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Response at 24 weeks, defined as menstrual blood loss ≤80 mL and a ≥50% reduction from baseline.
brief_rationale: In both placebo-controlled trials, every linzagolix regimen—with or without hormonal add-back therapy—produced a significantly higher primary-endpoint response rate than placebo (p≤0.003), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Objective response rate, defined as the proportion of treated randomly assigned patients achieving a complete or partial response by immune-related RECIST.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies objective response rate as the primary endpoint and reports response rates, but it does not state a prespecified response threshold, comparative hypothesis, or other criterion defining primary-endpoint success. Therefore, whether the endpoint met the trial's prespecified success criterion cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrence-free survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: Both active regimens significantly improved the explicitly identified primary endpoint versus placebo: nivolumab plus ipilimumab HR 0.25 (97.5% CI 0.13-0.48; p<0.0001) and nivolumab alone HR 0.60 (0.36-1.00; p=0.024).

primary_endpoint_description: Time to local recurrence
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was time to local recurrence. Tumour bed boost significantly reduced local recurrence versus no boost (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.31–0.72; p<0.001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients achieving an Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society 40 (ASAS40) response at week 14
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored upadacitinib over placebo: ASAS40 response occurred in 45% versus 23% of patients (treatment difference 22%, 95% CI 12–32; p<0.0001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints: PP-NRS4 response at week 2 and EASI-90 response at week 4.
brief_rationale: Abrocitinib produced significantly higher response rates than dupilumab for both primary endpoints: PP-NRS4 at week 2 (difference 22.6%; p<0.0001) and EASI-90 at week 4 (difference 14.1%; p<0.0001), under the stated sequential multiplicity-control procedure.

primary_endpoint_description: 3-year composite of cardiovascular death, major cardiovascular events, or non-fatal stroke in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 9.1% with combination therapy versus 9.9% with high-intensity statin monotherapy (absolute difference -0.78%; 90% CI -2.39% to 0.83%). The upper confidence bound was below the prespecified 2.0% noninferiority margin, meeting the noninferiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Modified Rankin Scale score of 0–2 at 90 days
brief_rationale: The lower limit of the one-sided 95% CI for the adjusted risk difference was -15.1%, crossing the prespecified noninferiority margin of -12%; therefore, thrombectomy alone did not demonstrate noninferiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Pain at 3 days post-randomisation measured using the Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale.
brief_rationale: The 95% confidence intervals for the adjusted between-group difference were within the prespecified equivalence margin of ±1.0 in both the modified intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses, establishing equivalence for the primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Safety and tolerability in all participants who received at least one dose of study drug
brief_rationale: The primary outcome was explicitly identified and safety findings were reported, including solicited and unsolicited adverse events and no vaccine-related serious adverse events. However, the abstract provides no prespecified threshold or other criterion defining success for safety and tolerability.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients in clinical remission (CDAI score <150) at week 52 in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 65% with ustekinumab versus 61% with adalimumab, but the between-group difference was not statistically significant (4%, 95% CI -6 to 14; p=0.42); therefore, favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of bleeding requiring invasive intervention, organ failure, and 90-day mortality
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite outcome occurred less often with algorithm-centred care than with usual care (8% vs 14%; adjusted RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38–0.61; p<0.0001), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival in all randomly assigned patients
brief_rationale: The prespecified primary endpoint was overall survival. Segmentectomy met the noninferiority criterion versus lobectomy: HR 0.663 (95% CI 0.474–0.927), with the CI upper limit below the prespecified margin of 1.54 and one-sided p<0.0001 for noninferiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Treatment difference in mean 24-hour systolic blood pressure at 6 months between renal denervation and sham control
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies the 6-month treatment difference in mean 24-hour systolic blood pressure as the primary endpoint, but reports efficacy results at 24 and 36 months without providing the 6-month primary-endpoint result.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding according to International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint is explicit and was reported, but the abstract does not state a prespecified success criterion or overall rule for the two asundexian dose comparisons. Results were mixed: the 20 mg confidence interval crossed 1, whereas the 50 mg and pooled estimates had upper 90% confidence limits below 1.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiovascular-related hospital admission, cardiovascular-related emergency department visit, or all-cause death within 12 months in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 15% of the low-sodium group versus 17% of the usual-care group (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.63–1.26; p=0.53), so the low-sodium intervention did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Malaria infection prevalence at 24 months after LLIN distribution, comparing each dual-active-ingredient LLIN group with the pyrethroid-only LLIN group in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The three primary treatment comparisons had mixed results: chlorfenapyr significantly reduced malaria prevalence, whereas pyriproxyfen and piperonyl butoxide did not. The abstract does not specify an overall success rule for these multiple comparisons, so a single trial-level determination is unclear.

primary_endpoint_description: Placebo-adjusted mean change in 24-hour cough frequency at week 12 in COUGH-1 and week 24 in COUGH-2.
brief_rationale: Gefapixant 45 mg twice daily significantly reduced 24-hour cough frequency versus placebo in both trials (COUGH-1: p=0.041; COUGH-2: p=0.031), meeting the favorable superiority criterion for the explicitly identified primary outcome. The 15 mg dose was not significant.

primary_endpoint_description: Hierarchical composite of cardiovascular death or non-fatal ischemic stroke at 12 months, total heart failure events through 24 months, and change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score at 12 months.
brief_rationale: The primary composite endpoint showed no difference between the atrial shunt and sham groups (win ratio 1.0, 95% CI 0.8–1.2; p=0.85), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Day 7 seven-category ordinal outcome assessing pulmonary status and extrapulmonary complications, ranging from no limiting symptoms to death
brief_rationale: The hIVIG group did not have significantly greater odds of a more favorable day 7 primary outcome than placebo (adjusted OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.77–1.45; p=0.72), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean change in best-corrected visual acuity from baseline averaged over weeks 40, 44, and 48, with a prespecified noninferiority margin of four letters
brief_rationale: Faricimab was explicitly reported as noninferior to aflibercept for the primary endpoint in both TENAYA and LUCERNE; the treatment-difference 95% CIs remained above the prespecified four-letter noninferiority boundary.

primary_endpoint_description: Rate of adverse events per 1000 patient-days
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome significantly favored the intervention: 22.6 versus 33.9 adverse events per 1000 patient-days (incidence rate ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.50–0.88; p=0.0048), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite at day 35 of symptomatic or fatal venous thromboembolism, asymptomatic venous thromboembolism detected by bilateral lower-limb ultrasound and CT pulmonary angiography, symptomatic arterial thromboembolism, and cardiovascular death
brief_rationale: The primary efficacy outcome occurred in 5/159 (3%) patients receiving rivaroxaban versus 15/159 (9%) receiving no anticoagulation (relative risk 0.33, 95% CI 0.12–0.90; p=0.0293), demonstrating statistically significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Efficacy of BBV152 in preventing a first occurrence of RT-PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 of any severity at least 14 days after the second dose in the per-protocol population.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored BBV152: 24 cases occurred among 8471 vaccine recipients versus 106 among 8502 placebo recipients, corresponding to vaccine efficacy of 77.8% (95% CI 65.2%–86.4%). The confidence interval demonstrated favorable efficacy over placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean serum bile acid change during the 4-week randomized withdrawal period among participants with at least a 50% serum bile acid reduction by week 18.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly states that the study met the primary endpoint, with a least-squares mean treatment difference of -117 μmol/L (95% CI -232 to -2), favoring continued maralixibat over withdrawal to placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: The 1-year rate of major adverse cardiac events, a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred less often with QFR guidance than with angiography guidance (5.8% vs 8.8%; HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.51-0.83; p=0.0004), demonstrating statistically significant benefit in the intended direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Surgical site infection (SSI), reported by trained outcome assessors.
brief_rationale: The primary outcome was SSI. Neither alcoholic chlorhexidine versus povidone-iodine nor triclosan-coated versus non-coated sutures significantly reduced SSI in either surgical-wound stratum or overall; the confidence intervals included no effect. Thus, the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Investigator-assessed disease-free survival, tested hierarchically in PD-L1-positive stage II–IIIA patients, all stage II–IIIA patients, and the stage IB–IIIA intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Atezolizumab significantly improved the primary disease-free survival endpoint versus best supportive care in the first hierarchical population (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50–0.88; p=0.0039) and subsequently in all stage II–IIIA patients (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.64–0.96; p=0.020), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI) score over 12 months
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome showed no favorable superiority for either factorial comparison: progressive exercise versus best practice advice (adjusted mean difference -0.66, 99% CI -4.52 to 3.20) and corticosteroid injection versus no injection (-1.11, 99% CI -4.47 to 2.26). Thus, the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Failure-free survival, defined as time from randomisation to disease recurrence (distant metastasis or locoregional recurrence) or death from any cause, in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored metronomic capecitabine: 3-year failure-free survival was 85.3% versus 75.7% with observation, with a stratified hazard ratio of 0.50 (95% CI 0.32-0.79; p=0.0023), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary week-16 endpoints: the proportion achieving at least 75% improvement in EASI (EASI-75) and the proportion achieving a vIGA-AD response (score 0 or 1 with at least a 2-grade reduction from baseline).
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly states that both coprimary endpoints were met in both placebo-controlled trials for both upadacitinib doses, with significantly higher response rates than placebo for EASI-75 and vIGA-AD response (all p<0.0001).

primary_endpoint_description: Change in daytime ambulatory systolic blood pressure at 2 months in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: Renal denervation produced a significantly greater reduction than sham in the explicitly identified primary endpoint (median between-group difference −4.5 mm Hg, 95% CI −8.5 to −0.3; adjusted p=0.022), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

This is explicitly a secondary health-status analysis. Although KCCQ is called the primary outcome for this secondary analysis, the abstract does not identify or report the original trial's prespecified primary endpoint, so trial-level primary-endpoint success cannot be assessed.

primary_endpoint_description: 28-day mortality
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Mortality was 24% in both groups (rate ratio 1.00, 95% CI 0.93–1.07; p=0.95), so convalescent plasma did not demonstrate favorable superiority over usual care.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of participants in each sonelokimab group achieving an Investigator's Global Assessment score of clear or almost clear (IGA 0 or 1) at week 12 compared with placebo.
brief_rationale: At week 12, IGA 0 or 1 was achieved by 48.1% to 88.2% of participants across the sonelokimab groups versus 0% with placebo; every sonelokimab-placebo comparison was significant (p<0.0001), demonstrating favorable superiority on the explicitly identified primary outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy outcome: viral suppression (HIV-1 RNA <200 copies/mL) at or within 14 days of delivery; primary safety outcomes: composite adverse pregnancy outcome and grade 3 or higher maternal and infant adverse events.
brief_rationale: The efficacy endpoint met its prespecified noninferiority criterion, with the 95% CI excluding the -10% margin. However, multiple primary safety outcomes were also designated: the composite pregnancy outcome favored one dolutegravir regimen in pairwise comparisons, while grade ≥3 adverse events did not differ. No overall success rule integrating the efficacy and safety primary outcomes is stated.

This is explicitly described as a post-hoc exploratory variant analysis. Although efficacy against symptomatic NAAT-positive infection is reported, the abstract does not explicitly identify it as the trial's prespecified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Two coprimary endpoints within 28 days: time to first self-reported recovery and COVID-19-related hospital admission or death.
brief_rationale: Azithromycin did not demonstrate a clinically meaningful benefit for either coprimary endpoint: the probability of at least a 1.5-day recovery benefit was 0.23, and COVID-19-related hospitalization or death was not reduced meaningfully.

The abstract explicitly describes a noninferiority trial and reports that malaria incidence met the noninferiority margin, but it does not explicitly identify malaria incidence—or any other measure—as the primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival (PFS)
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was PFS. Cabozantinib significantly prolonged PFS versus sunitinib (median 9.0 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37–0.97; one-sided p=0.019), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: PSA response, defined as a reduction of at least 50% from baseline
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint occurred more frequently with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 than with cabazitaxel in the intention-to-treat analysis (66% vs 37%; difference 29%, 95% CI 16–42; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: 28-day all-cause mortality in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 22% of both groups (rate ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.87–1.07; p=0.50), so azithromycin did not demonstrate superior survival versus usual care.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was progression-free survival, which was significantly longer with adavosertib plus gemcitabine than with placebo plus gemcitabine (median 4.6 vs 3.0 months; HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.35–0.90; log-rank p=0.015), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Safety through 28 days after each dose, including solicited and serious adverse events, and day-28 seroprotection rates after the first dose, comparing monovalent OPV2 with the two novel OPV2 candidates.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies safety and immunogenicity as primary objectives and reports generally favorable findings, but it does not provide prespecified superiority, noninferiority, equivalence, or other quantitative success criteria. Therefore, whether the primary endpoints formally met trial success criteria cannot be determined.

This secondary model-development and validation analysis does not explicitly identify or report the randomized trial's prespecified primary endpoint. The reported 10-year mortality and 5-year major adverse cardiovascular event prediction metrics therefore cannot be used to determine primary-endpoint success.

primary_endpoint_description: Net adverse clinical events at 1 year, comprising all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularisation, stroke, and BARC grade 2 or higher bleeding
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 7.2% of the de-escalation group versus 10.1% of the conventional group. With a prespecified absolute noninferiority margin of 2.5%, noninferiority was met (absolute risk difference -2.9%; p<0.0001 for noninferiority).

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary week-12 endpoints: Investigator Global Assessment response (score 0 or 1 with at least a 2-grade improvement) and at least 75% improvement in EASI score (EASI-75).
brief_rationale: Both abrocitinib doses produced significantly higher week-12 response rates than placebo for both coprimary endpoints (IGA: p=0.0037 and p<0.0001; EASI-75: p<0.0001 for both doses), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Day-28 GMTs of RBD-specific ELISA antibodies and neutralising antibodies, plus incidence of adverse reactions within 14 days
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies immunogenicity and safety primary endpoints and reports their results, but it does not state prespecified thresholds, comparison criteria, or an overall success rule for determining whether these endpoints were met.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary outcomes: efficacy measured by symptomatic, virologically confirmed COVID-19 cases, and safety measured by serious adverse events.
brief_rationale: This preliminary report states that the trial is ongoing and does not report the co-primary efficacy outcome. Although no serious adverse events related to ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 occurred, the full co-primary endpoint assessment and overall success rule cannot be evaluated.

primary_endpoint_description: Total length of hospital stay, including readmission, up to 30 days after randomisation
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored ambulatory care: median hospitalization was 0 days versus 4 days with standard care, a statistically significant reduction (p<0.0001; median difference 2 days, 95% CI 1–3).

primary_endpoint_description: Primary safety endpoint: composite of all-cause mortality, disabling stroke, life-threatening bleeding requiring transfusion, acute kidney injury requiring dialysis, or major vascular complication at 30 days; primary efficacy endpoint: all-cause mortality or disabling stroke at 1 year.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints met their noninferiority criteria. For safety, the upper confidence bound was 8.1%, below the 8.5% margin (p_noninferiority=0.034); for efficacy, it was 5.7%, below the 8.0% margin (p_noninferiority=0.0058).

primary_endpoint_description: Ipsilateral breast tumour relapse at 5 years
brief_rationale: Both five-fraction schedules met the prespecified noninferiority criterion versus 40 Gy in 15 fractions: the upper 95% CI limits for the hazard ratios were 1.44 for 27 Gy and 1.16 for 26 Gy, both below the critical HR margin of 1.81.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to clinical improvement up to day 28, defined as a two-level decline on the six-point clinical-status scale or live hospital discharge, whichever occurred first.
brief_rationale: Remdesivir did not significantly improve the explicitly identified primary endpoint versus placebo (hazard ratio 1.23, 95% CI 0.87–1.75), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrence-free survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: At the prespecified interim analysis, recurrence-free survival was significantly improved versus placebo with both nivolumab plus ipilimumab (HR 0.23, 97.5% CI 0.12–0.45; p<0.0001) and nivolumab monotherapy (HR 0.56, 97.5% CI 0.33–0.94; p=0.011), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time from the start of study treatment to a nasopharyngeal swab negative for SARS-CoV-2 by RT-PCR in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored combination therapy: median time to a negative swab was 7 days versus 12 days with control (hazard ratio 4.37, 95% CI 1.86–10.24; p=0.0010), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients achieving an ACR20 response at week 52, testing superiority of secukinumab versus adalimumab
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint did not meet the superiority criterion: ACR20 response was 67% with secukinumab versus 62% with adalimumab (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.98–1.72; p=0.0719).

primary_endpoint_description: Baseline-adjusted change in 24-hour systolic blood pressure from baseline to 3 months after the procedure
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint was met: renal denervation reduced 24-hour systolic blood pressure versus sham by 3.9 mm Hg (95% Bayesian credible interval 1.6 to 6.2 mm Hg in the favorable direction), with a posterior probability of superiority greater than 0.999.

primary_endpoint_description: Neutralising geometric mean antibody titres for each of the four dengue serotypes through month 48 in the per-protocol immunogenicity subset.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies assessment of neutralising geometric mean titres as the primary objective and reports elevated titres versus placebo at month 48, but it does not state a prespecified statistical threshold or other success criterion for this endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: American College of Rheumatology 20% improvement (ACR20) response at week 24
brief_rationale: Both guselkumab regimens produced significantly higher week-24 ACR20 response rates than placebo (64% vs 33%; both p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion for the explicitly identified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: American College of Rheumatology 20% improvement response (ACR20) at week 24 in all patients by assigned treatment group, using non-responder imputation.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly states that the primary endpoint was met. ACR20 response rates were significantly higher with guselkumab every 4 weeks (59%) and every 8 weeks (52%) than with placebo (22%); both comparisons had p<0.0001.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients achieving at least 50% improvement in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (ACR50) at week 12
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored bimekizumab: significantly more patients achieved ACR50 versus placebo with 16 mg, 160 mg, and 160 mg plus a 320 mg loading dose (p=0.032, 0.0012, and 0.0004, respectively).

primary_endpoint_description: Incidence of preterm birth, defined as delivery before 37 weeks' gestational age
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less often with low-dose aspirin than placebo (11.6% vs 13.1%; RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.81-0.98; p=0.012), demonstrating statistically significant benefit in the intended direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients with microbiological cure of urogenital Neisseria gonorrhoeae at test of cure (day 6 ± 2) in the microbiological intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The comparator-minus-zoliflodacin difference was 5.3% (95% CI 1.4%–8.6%); the upper CI bound of 8.6% was below the prespecified 12% noninferiority margin, so the primary endpoint met the success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Dual primary endpoints of independent review committee-assessed overall response rate and progression-free survival.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly states that the trial met both primary endpoints and demonstrated superiority of epcoritamab plus R2 over R2: overall response rate was 95% versus 79% (p<0.0001), and progression-free survival favored epcoritamab plus R2 (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.14–0.31; p<0.0001).

primary_endpoint_description: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population of all randomized patients.
brief_rationale: In the planned primary analysis, tafasitamab plus lenalidomide and rituximab significantly improved progression-free survival versus placebo plus lenalidomide and rituximab (median 22.4 vs 13.9 months; HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.32–0.58; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in pain Numeric Rating Scale score from baseline to 10 minutes after treatment initiation, analysed per protocol.
brief_rationale: With a prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.3 NRS points, methoxyflurane was reported as noninferior to both intranasal fentanyl and intravenous morphine at 10 minutes. Thus, the primary noninferiority objective for methoxyflurane was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Solicited and unsolicited adverse events, clinically significant laboratory test abnormalities, medically attended adverse events, and serious adverse events.
brief_rationale: The primary safety endpoints are explicit, and the abstract reports mostly mild-to-moderate injection-site pain with no serious adverse events, hospitalisations, or deaths. However, it provides no prespecified threshold or other overall success criterion for these safety endpoints, so primary-endpoint success cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Investigator-assessed event-free survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: At the prespecified interim analysis, perioperative camrelizumab plus rivoceranib significantly improved the primary endpoint of event-free survival versus surgery alone (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.41–0.85; p=0.0040), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival assessed by an independent radiographic review committee according to RECIST version 1.1 in all randomly assigned patients.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored ivonescimab plus chemotherapy: median progression-free survival was 11.1 versus 6.9 months, with a hazard ratio of 0.60 (95% CI 0.46-0.78; one-sided p<0.0001), demonstrating statistically significant superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of sterile blood cultures at day 3 (day 5 for endocarditis) without bacteraemia relapse, survival, and clinical success at day 90 in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The prespecified noninferiority margin was 12%. The primary endpoint occurred in 75% with cefazolin versus 74% with cloxacillin; the treatment difference was -1% (95% CI -11% to 9%), so the lower confidence bound remained within the -12% margin, meeting noninferiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation (composite endpoint).
brief_rationale: The primary composite endpoint was explicitly identified and was not statistically significant: HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.83–1.04; p=0.22). Thus, vericiguat did not demonstrate superiority over placebo for the primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite endpoint occurred less often with vericiguat than placebo (25.9% vs 27.9%; HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.98; p=0.0088), demonstrating statistically significant benefit in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Total SNOT-22 quality-of-life score at 6 months after randomisation
brief_rationale: For the primary outcome, endoscopic sinus surgery produced significantly lower (better) 6-month SNOT-22 scores than clarithromycin and placebo at the Bonferroni-adjusted 98.33% confidence level (both p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion. Clarithromycin was not superior to placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival in this randomized superiority trial. Chemotherapy plus hormonotherapy did not significantly improve overall survival versus hormonotherapy alone (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.63–1.11; stratified log-rank p=0.2100), so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary outcomes were individual-level prevalence and cluster-level transmission interruption (weighted prevalence of the predominant soil-transmitted helminth species ≤2%) 24 months after the last MDA round.
brief_rationale: Community-wide MDA significantly reduced individual-level prevalence versus school-based deworming in all three countries, but cluster-level transmission interruption did not differ significantly. Because the co-primary outcomes had mixed results and no overall success rule is stated, trial success is unclear.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26, with a non-inferiority margin of 0.4 percentage points.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies HbA1c change through week 26 as the primary endpoint and reports that the between-group result established non-inferiority of once-weekly efsitora versus glargine U100 under the prespecified 0.4% margin.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in least-squares mean HbA1c concentration from baseline to week 26, with a non-inferiority margin of 0.4% for efsitora versus degludec.
brief_rationale: The estimated treatment difference was -0.09 percentage points (95% CI -0.19 to 0.01), satisfying the prespecified 0.4% non-inferiority margin and indicating non-inferiority of efsitora to degludec.

primary_endpoint_description: Number of treatment-emergent adverse events from baseline to end of study across Parts A-E
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint was explicitly identified as the number of treatment-emergent adverse events. Although adverse events were described qualitatively, the abstract states no prespecified threshold or other criterion defining success for this safety endpoint, so whether it was met cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Objective response rate (confirmed partial or complete response) by cycle 16, assessed by independent central review using REiNS criteria
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored selumetinib: objective response rate was 20% (14/71) versus 5% (4/74) with placebo, with a statistically significant between-group difference (p=0.011).

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival assessed by an independent review committee in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored satri-cel: median progression-free survival was 3.25 versus 1.77 months, with a hazard ratio of 0.37 (95% CI 0.24–0.56) and one-sided log-rank p<0.0001, demonstrating significant superiority over physician's choice.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival in all randomly assigned patients
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint, overall survival, was significantly improved with nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus lenvatinib or sorafenib (median 23.7 vs 20.6 months; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65-0.96; p=0.018), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints were percent changes in LDL cholesterol at day 84 for the fixed-dose combination versus placebo, ezetimibe monotherapy, and obicetrapib monotherapy, plus placebo-adjusted change with obicetrapib monotherapy.
brief_rationale: All co-primary comparisons favored active treatment: the fixed-dose combination reduced LDL cholesterol versus placebo, ezetimibe, and obicetrapib, with all 95% CIs excluding no difference; obicetrapib monotherapy also reduced LDL cholesterol versus placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death, stroke, moderate or severe aortic regurgitation, or moderate or severe haemodynamic transcatheter heart valve deterioration at 1 year
brief_rationale: The prespecified noninferiority margin was 5.3%. The primary endpoint risk difference was -0.9%, with a one-sided upper 95% CI of 4.4%, which was below the margin (p for noninferiority=0.019); thus Myval met the noninferiority criterion versus SAPIEN 3.

primary_endpoint_description: Ratio to baseline of maximum walking distance at week 52, measured on a constant-load treadmill
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored semaglutide over placebo, with an estimated treatment ratio of 1.13 (95% CI 1.06–1.21; p=0.0004), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Colorectal cancer mortality at 10 years in the intention-to-screen population
brief_rationale: The prespecified primary endpoint was 10-year colorectal cancer mortality, with an absolute difference of less than 0.16 percentage points required for noninferiority. Faecal immunochemical testing met this criterion versus colonoscopy (reported risk difference -0.02 percentage points, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.06; p for noninferiority=0.0005).

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival assessed by a masked independent radiographic review committee per RECIST v1.1 in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: At the preplanned interim analysis, the explicitly identified primary endpoint favored ivonescimab: median PFS was 11.1 versus 5.8 months, with HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.38–0.69) and one-sided p<0.0001, meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints: change from baseline in total endoscopic nasal polyps score at week 52 and mean nasal obstruction score over weeks 49–52.
brief_rationale: Depemokimab significantly improved both coprimary endpoints versus placebo in both ANCHOR-1 and ANCHOR-2, with all reported p values below 0.05 and effects in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism, including recurrent fatal or non-fatal pulmonary embolism or isolated proximal deep vein thrombosis
brief_rationale: The reduced-dose regimen did not meet the prespecified noninferiority criterion versus full-dose treatment (adjusted HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.67–2.60; noninferiority margin HR 1.7; p=0.23 for noninferiority).

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints of first ischaemic stroke and first recurrent intracerebral haemorrhage
brief_rationale: The ischaemic-stroke coprimary endpoint met superiority (HR 0.05, 95% CI 0.01–0.36; p<0.0001), whereas the recurrent-intracerebral-haemorrhage coprimary endpoint failed the prespecified noninferiority margin (HR 10.89, 90% CI 1.95–60.72). The abstract reports hierarchical testing but does not clearly state the overall trial success rule for these mixed coprimary results.

primary_endpoint_description: Comparison of ordinal modified Rankin Scale scores at 90 days in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The primary outcome favored normobaric hyperoxia plus endovascular treatment over sham plus endovascular treatment (adjusted common odds ratio 1.65, 95% CI 1.09–2.50; p=0.018), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: MDS-UPDRS part III score off dopaminergic medication at 96 weeks
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint worsened by 5.7 points with exenatide versus 4.5 points with placebo. The adjusted treatment effect was 0.92 (95% CI -1.56 to 3.39; p=0.47), so exenatide did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of coronary heart disease death or non-fatal myocardial infarction at 10 years
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred less frequently with CCTA-guided care than with standard care (6.6% vs 8.2%; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63–0.99; p=0.044), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to treatment failure, defined as recurrence of uveitis or arthritis.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint significantly favored continued adalimumab: treatment failure occurred in 68% after discontinuation (placebo) versus 14% with adalimumab (HR 8.7, 95% CI 3.6–21.2; p<0.0001). Thus, discontinuation did not succeed in the intended favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review per RECIST version 1.1 for durvalumab plus bevacizumab versus placebo alone in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored durvalumab plus bevacizumab: median progression-free survival was 15.0 versus 8.2 months, with a hazard ratio of 0.77 (95% CI 0.61-0.98; two-sided p=0.032), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Co-primary endpoints of blinded-independent-central-review progression-free survival and overall survival in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Progression-free survival met its stated threshold (HR 0.66; one-sided p=0.0002 vs 0.025), whereas overall survival did not at this interim analysis (HR 0.80; one-sided p=0.087 vs 0.0012). The abstract does not state the overall success rule for these co-primary endpoints.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints of radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival, assessed in patients with low-volume metastatic disease and in the overall study population.
brief_rationale: Radiotherapy improved radiographic progression-free survival in the low-volume subgroup receiving abiraterone but not in those not receiving abiraterone, while overall survival in low-volume disease was not improved. Results for the overall study population and an overall success rule for the coprimary endpoints are not provided, so trial success cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. At the primary analysis, Glofit-GemOx significantly improved overall survival versus R-GemOx (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.40–0.89; p=0.011), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of death, myocardial infarction, and unplanned revascularisation at 12 months
brief_rationale: The 12-month event-rate difference was 2.5% with a two-sided 90% CI of 0.9% to 4.2%. Because the upper CI limit exceeded the prespecified 3.4% noninferiority margin, QFR did not meet noninferiority to FFR.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean change from baseline in blood phenylalanine concentration after 6 weeks in part 2
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint showed a significantly greater reduction with sepiapterin than placebo (least-squares mean difference -395.9 μmol/L; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Radiographic progression-free survival, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression or death, assessed in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The primary analysis showed significantly longer radiographic progression-free survival with 177Lu-PSMA-617 than with ARPI change (median 9.30 vs 5.55 months; HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.29-0.56; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

This is a post-hoc pooled analysis that identifies three 'main outcomes' but does not explicitly identify a prespecified primary endpoint or report the original trials' primary endpoints sufficiently for assessment.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of day-care procedures, defined as abortion completed in less than 9 hours
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored home administration: 71% versus 46% completed abortion as day-care patients, with a difference of 24.9% (95% CI 15.4–34.3; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to first event within 30 days after transplantation of a composite of cardiac-related death, moderate or severe left ventricular primary graft dysfunction, right ventricular primary graft dysfunction, acute cellular rejection of at least grade 2R, or graft failure requiring mechanical circulatory support or retransplantation.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary composite endpoint occurred in 19% with HOPE versus 30% with static cold storage (hazard ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.32–0.99), but the log-rank p value was 0.059. The abstract explicitly states that the primary endpoint difference was not significant; therefore, the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Baseline-adjusted EQ-5D-5L health utility score assessed at 30, 90, and 180 days after randomisation.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint significantly favored standard protein rather than the intended high-protein intervention: mean difference −0.05 (95% CI −0.10 to −0.01; p=0.031). Thus, favorable superiority was not achieved.

primary_endpoint_description: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored molecularly guided therapy: median progression-free survival was 6.1 versus 4.4 months, with a hazard ratio of 0.72 (95% CI 0.56-0.92; p=0.0079), demonstrating statistically significant superiority over chemotherapy.

primary_endpoint_description: Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) response rate at week 12
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored digital ACT: 71% responded versus 22% with active control, a difference of 48.4% (95% CI 37.9–58.9; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Hierarchical coprimary objectives of improved tolerability, defined by treatment-related morbidity, and noninferior efficacy, defined by progression-free survival with a 6-percentage-point absolute noninferiority margin.
brief_rationale: Both hierarchical coprimary objectives succeeded: treatment-related morbidity was significantly lower with BrECADD (42% vs 59%; p<0.0001), and progression-free survival met noninferiority, permitting the prespecified superiority test, which also favored BrECADD (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45–0.97; p=0.035).

primary_endpoint_description: Days to the first recurrence of an activity-limiting episode of low back pain
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored the walking and education intervention: recurrence hazard ratio 0.72 (95% CI 0.60–0.85; p=0.0002), with median time to recurrence of 208 versus 112 days. This met the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of first fatal or non-fatal recurrent ischaemic stroke, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, or hospitalisation for unstable angina.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored colchicine numerically but did not meet the prespecified superiority threshold of p<0.048 (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.68–1.05; p=0.12).

primary_endpoint_description: Ankle function measured by the Olerud and Molander Ankle Score (OMAS) at 4 months after randomisation in the per-protocol population.
brief_rationale: The prespecified noninferiority margin was -6 OMAS points. The adjusted difference favored early weight-bearing by 4.47 points (95% CI 0.58 to 8.37), so the confidence interval remained above the noninferiority margin and the primary endpoint met the noninferiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, ischaemia-driven target-vessel revascularisation, or hospitalisation for unstable or progressive angina at 2 years
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred in 0.4% of the preventive PCI group versus 3.4% of the optimal medical therapy group, an absolute difference of -3.0 percentage points (95% CI -4.4 to -1.8; p=0.0003), demonstrating significant superiority in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Myocardial blood flow in myocardial segments designated ischaemic at enrolment, and the primary symptom outcome of daily angina episode frequency, both assessed at 6 months
brief_rationale: CSR did not improve myocardial blood flow versus placebo (difference 0.06 mL/min/g; 95% CrI −0.09 to 0.20), whereas daily angina episodes improved (OR 1.40; 95% CrI 1.08 to 1.83). Because the explicitly identified primary outcomes had mixed results and no overall success rule is stated, trial success is unclear.

primary_endpoint_description: Dual primary endpoints: change from baseline to week 52 in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS) and bodyweight.
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary endpoints favored semaglutide over placebo: KCCQ-CSS improved by a between-group difference of 7.5 points (95% CI 5.3 to 9.8; p<0.0001), and bodyweight was reduced by 8.4% more (95% CI -9.2 to -7.5; p<0.0001). Thus, both dual primary superiority endpoints met their success criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: All-cause mortality excluding injury; hospital admission with severe malaria, meningitis, or cerebral malaria; deaths in girls compared with boys; and vaccination coverage.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies several primary impact, safety, and feasibility outcomes and reports generally favorable findings, but it does not state an overall success rule or prespecified criterion for combining these outcomes, particularly vaccination coverage and mortality. Overall primary-endpoint success is therefore indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: 3-year invasive disease-free survival in patients in group B
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies 3-year iDFS in group B as a primary endpoint and reports a 94.8% rate (95% CI 91.4–97.1; p=0.001), explicitly stating that this met the primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Lot-to-lot equivalence of three nOPV2 lots based on one-dose type 2 poliovirus neutralising antibody seroconversion rates in infants.
brief_rationale: Equivalence required the 95% CIs for all three pairwise seroconversion-rate differences to lie within −10% to 10%. The observed bounds ranged from −5.8% to 5.4%, so the prespecified equivalence criterion was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Ordinal modified Rankin Scale score distribution at 1-year follow-up in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome significantly favored thrombectomy plus medical care over medical care alone (probability of superiority 0.59, 95% CI 0.53–0.64; p=0.0019; generalized odds ratio 1.43, 95% CI 1.14–1.78), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Live birth after the first embryo transfer
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 33.8% of couples assigned to ICSI versus 36.6% assigned to conventional IVF (adjusted RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.83–1.03; p=0.16). ICSI did not demonstrate favorable superiority over conventional IVF.

primary_endpoint_description: First occurrence of blood culture-confirmed typhoid fever
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 24 Vi-TT recipients versus 110 MenA control recipients. Vi-TT efficacy was 78.3% (95% CI 66.3%–86.1%), demonstrating statistically significant protection in the favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline to week 5 in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored KarXT over placebo: least-squares mean difference −9.6 points (95% CI −13.9 to −5.2; p<0.0001). The abstract states that the trial met its primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Duration of organ support at 30 days after random allocation, using a rank-based endpoint that assigned death by day 30 as the worst outcome.
brief_rationale: The conservative oxygenation group had a significantly better primary outcome than the liberal group (probabilistic index 0.53, 95% CI 0.50–0.55; p=0.04), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Neonatal morbidity at birth, defined as a composite of umbilical arterial pH <7.10, base excess >10 mmol/L, umbilical arterial lactate >7 mmol/L, 5-minute Apgar score <7, or neonatal intensive care unit admission.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome occurred in 9.6% of the discontinuation group versus 9.2% of the continuous-oxytocin group (absolute difference 0.4%, 95% CI −2.1 to 2.9; RR 1.0, 95% CI 0.8 to 1.4). Discontinuation did not significantly reduce neonatal morbidity, so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival in all randomly assigned patients
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival versus chemotherapy alone (HR for death 0.79, 95% CI 0.64–0.98; two-sided p=0.0324), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Recurrence-free survival by independent review facility assessment in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was significantly improved with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab versus active surveillance at the prespecified interim analysis (HR 0.72, adjusted 95% CI 0.53–0.98; p=0.012), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change from baseline to month 12 in total geographic atrophy lesion area in the study eye measured by fundus autofluorescence imaging.
brief_rationale: Primary-endpoint results were mixed across the two trials: both pegcetacoplan regimens significantly reduced lesion growth versus sham in OAKS, but neither was significant in DERBY. No overall success rule combining the trials or comparisons is stated.

primary_endpoint_description: Pain reduction in the study hand at 6 months, measured using a 100 mm visual analogue scale
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored methotrexate: the between-group difference in VAS pain change was -9.9 mm (95% CI -19.3 to -0.6; p=0.037), demonstrating statistically significant superiority over placebo in pain reduction.

primary_endpoint_description: Functional outcome across the entire modified Rankin Scale distribution at 90 days
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored endovascular thrombectomy, with a significant shift toward better modified Rankin Scale outcomes (adjusted common OR 2.58, 95% CI 1.60–4.15; p=0.0001); the trial was stopped early for efficacy.

primary_endpoint_description: Sustained platelet count response (platelet count ≥50 × 10^9/L for at least 4 of the last 6 weeks) in the chronic immune thrombocytopenia population.
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint was achieved by 22% of efgartigimod-treated patients versus 5% receiving placebo, a favorable significant difference (p=0.032; adjusted difference 16% [95% CI 2.6–26.4]).

primary_endpoint_description: Geographic atrophy lesion size measured by fundus autofluorescence at baseline, month 6, and month 12
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint showed significantly slower geographic atrophy area growth with avacincaptad pegol than with sham through month 12 (difference 0.056 mm/year, 95% CI 0.016–0.096; p=0.0064), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: All-cause mortality at 30 days
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint occurred in 63% of both groups, with no evidence of improved survival from expedited transfer (unadjusted risk ratio for survival 1.00, 95% CI 0.90–1.11; p=0.96). The favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Progression-free survival
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies progression-free survival as the primary endpoint and states that sacituzumab govitecan demonstrated a significant progression-free survival benefit over chemotherapy. Although previously reported and not part of the current overall-survival analysis, the reported favorable significant result supports primary-endpoint success.

primary_endpoint_description: Participation rate and yield of the home-based screening and elaborate screening.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies participation rate and yield across home-based and elaborate screening as primary outcomes, but it does not state an overall success rule or prespecified thresholds for these multiple outcomes. Although participation was higher with the urine collection device, the reported findings do not establish whether the trial's primary-endpoint success criterion was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was overall survival. Atezolizumab significantly improved overall survival versus chemotherapy (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.97; p=0.028), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 52, evaluated with a treatment policy estimand in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Both higher doses achieved significantly greater HbA1c reductions than 14 mg at week 52: ETD −0.27 percentage points for 25 mg (95% CI −0.42 to −0.12; p=0.0006) and −0.53 for 50 mg (95% CI −0.68 to −0.38; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints were percent change in bodyweight from baseline and achievement of at least 5% bodyweight reduction at week 72.
brief_rationale: Both tirzepatide doses produced significantly greater mean percentage weight loss than placebo (p<0.0001), and substantially more participants achieved at least 5% weight reduction (79–83% vs 32%), supporting favorable superiority on both coprimary endpoints.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean change in HbA1c from baseline at week 26 with orforglipron versus placebo.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies this as the primary efficacy outcome and reports that HbA1c reduction with orforglipron was statistically superior to placebo, with estimated treatment differences favoring orforglipron of -0.8% to -1.7%.

primary_endpoint_description: Ipsilateral breast tumour relapse (IBTR), analysed by intention to treat, with noninferiority defined as no more than a 3% absolute excess versus control based on the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI.
brief_rationale: Results were mixed across the two test-group comparisons: test group 1 met the noninferiority criterion (upper CI 1.7%), whereas test group 2 did not (upper CI 3.8%). The abstract does not specify an overall success rule for these multiple comparisons.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean between-group difference in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score at 12 months
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored haemodynamic monitoring, with a mean between-group difference in change of 7.13 points (95% CI 1.51–12.75; p=0.013), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival, defined as time from randomisation until death from any cause, assessed in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored quizartinib: median overall survival was 31.9 months versus 15.1 months with placebo (hazard ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.98; p=0.032), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Maternal anaemia prevalence at 36 weeks' gestation and neonatal birthweight
brief_rationale: Both explicitly identified primary outcomes failed to show superiority: anaemia prevalence at 36 weeks was not significantly reduced (PR 0.92, 95% CI 0.81–1.06; p=0.27), and birthweight did not differ between groups (mean difference −3.1 g, 95% CI −75.0 to 68.9; p=0.93).

primary_endpoint_description: Overall survival in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: Overall survival favored pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin versus placebo plus chemotherapy (median 12.7 vs 10.9 months; HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72–0.95). The one-sided p=0.0034 met the prespecified significance threshold of p=0.0200.

primary_endpoint_description: Length-for-age Z score at 12 months and Bayley-III cognitive composite score at 6 and 12 months
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies these as primary outcomes and states that vitamin B12 had no effect on them. Reported between-group differences were not favorably significant, so the superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Rate of solicited and unsolicited adverse events through study day 56
brief_rationale: The primary safety endpoint was reported, including adverse-event rates and no serious adverse events, but the abstract does not state a prespecified threshold or other formal criterion for primary-endpoint success.
The abstract reports feasibility, acceptability, attrition, and app engagement measures but does not explicitly identify any measure as the prespecified primary endpoint or primary outcome.

primary_endpoint_description: Composite adverse pregnancy outcome: fetal loss, adverse newborn outcomes (small for gestational age, low birthweight, or preterm birth), or neonatal death.
brief_rationale: The primary composite occurred significantly more often, not less often, with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine alone (27.9% vs 23.3%; RR 1.20, 95% CI 1.06–1.36) and with added azithromycin (27.6% vs 23.3%; RR 1.16, 95% CI 1.03–1.32) than with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. Thus, neither intervention achieved favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of participants with a modified Rankin Scale score of 0–1 at 90 days in the modified intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: The risk ratio was 1.07 (95% CI 0.98–1.16); the lower confidence limit exceeded the prespecified noninferiority margin of 0.937, so the primary efficacy endpoint met the noninferiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to use of conventional attack treatment within 12 hours of study drug administration
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint significantly favored sebetralstat over placebo: time to conventional treatment was longer (quartile 1, >12 h vs 8.0 h; p=0.0010), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Occurrence of clinically relevant adverse drug reactions within the 12-week follow-up period
brief_rationale: The prespecified gatekeeping primary analysis first compared participants with an actionable drug-gene interaction. Clinically relevant adverse drug reactions were significantly less frequent with genotype-guided treatment than with control (21.0% vs 27.7%; OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.54-0.91; p=0.0075), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: MFSAF total symptom score response rate at week 24, defined as at least a 50% reduction from baseline in mean MFSAF total symptom score over the preceding 28 days.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored momelotinib: response occurred in 25% versus 9% with danazol, with a proportion difference of 16% (95% CI 6–26; p=0.0095), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Safety and tolerability of multiple ascending doses of emraclidine, assessed in participants receiving at least one dose of study treatment
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint is explicitly identified and safety findings are reported, including similar adverse-event incidence across groups. However, the abstract provides no prespecified threshold or other explicit criterion defining successful safety and tolerability, so primary-endpoint success cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients achieving at least 50% improvement in American College of Rheumatology criteria (ACR50) at week 16, using non-responder imputation.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies week-16 ACR50 response as the primary endpoint and states that it was met. ACR50 was achieved by 43% with bimekizumab versus 7% with placebo (adjusted OR 11.1, 95% CI 5.4–23.0; p<0.0001), demonstrating favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients achieving at least 50% improvement in American College of Rheumatology criteria (ACR50) at week 16
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored bimekizumab over placebo: 44% versus 10% achieved ACR50 at week 16 (odds ratio 7.1, 95% CI 4.6–10.9; p<0.0001), meeting the superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Pregnancy loss, defined as miscarriage, stillbirth, or neonatal death in the first week of life
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 8.0% with monofilament versus 7.6% with braided suture (adjusted risk ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.79–1.40). Monofilament suture did not demonstrate the intended favorable superiority in reducing pregnancy loss.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in office systolic blood pressure from baseline to 6 months in the renal artery denervation group compared with the sham-control group.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies this as the original primary endpoint and states that the trial did not show efficacy at 6 months; therefore, the favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of patients with an Investigator's Global Assessment score of 0–1 (clear or almost clear skin) at week 16.
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored dupilumab: IGA 0–1 at week 16 occurred in 28% versus 4% with placebo (difference 24%, 95% CI 13–34; p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score-4 domain version (KOOS4) at 18 months after randomisation
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome favored surgical reconstruction: adjusted mean KOOS4 difference 7.9 points (95% CI 2.5 to 13.2; p=0.0053). In this stated superiority trial, the favorable superiority criterion was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Need for exogenous intratracheal surfactant within 48 hours after birth
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 20.0% of the half-dose group and 17.5% of the full-dose group (risk difference 2.4%, 95% CI −0.3 to 5.2). The upper confidence limit exceeded the prespecified 4-percentage-point noninferiority margin, so noninferiority was not shown.

primary_endpoint_description: 28-day mortality in the intention-to-treat population
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Mortality was significantly lower with baricitinib than with usual care (12% vs 14%; age-adjusted rate ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.77-0.99; p=0.028), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage of excess weight loss at 52 weeks
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint favored ESG: mean excess weight loss at 52 weeks was 49.2% with ESG plus lifestyle modification versus 3.2% with lifestyle modification alone (p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Development of clinical arthritis (fulfilling the 2010 rheumatoid arthritis classification criteria or involving at least two joints) persisting for at least 2 weeks
brief_rationale: At 2 years, the primary endpoint occurred at a similar frequency with methotrexate and placebo (19% vs 18%; hazard ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.45–1.48), so favorable superiority was not demonstrated.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical remission per Adapted Mayo score at week 8 in the two induction studies and at week 52 in the maintenance study.
brief_rationale: All explicitly identified primary endpoints favored upadacitinib over placebo and were statistically significant: week 8 remission in UC1 and UC2 and week 52 remission for both maintenance doses (all p<0.0001).

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints of clinical remission (defined by CDAI or patient-reported stool-frequency and abdominal-pain criteria) and endoscopic response at week 12
brief_rationale: The placebo-controlled trials explicitly identified these as coprimary endpoints and reported that all were met at week 12 in both ADVANCE and MOTIVATE with both risankizumab doses, with favorable differences versus placebo and p≤0.0001.

primary_endpoint_description: Protocol-specified in-hospital mortality, subdivided by disease severity
brief_rationale: For remdesivir, overall in-hospital mortality was 14.5% versus 15.6% with control (mortality RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.82–1.02; p=0.12), so favorable superiority on the primary endpoint was not established. Favorable findings in selected severity groups or the non-prespecified composite do not change the primary-endpoint assessment.

primary_endpoint_description: Oxford Shoulder Score at 12 months
brief_rationale: The device group had a significantly worse primary outcome than the debridement-only control group (adjusted mean difference -4.2, 95% CI -8.2 to -0.26; p=0.037), favoring control. Thus, the primary superiority endpoint did not succeed in the intended favorable direction.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical efficacy of EV71vac against EV71-associated diseases in the total vaccinated cohort during the specified follow-up period
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary efficacy endpoint favored EV71vac, with vaccine efficacy of 96.8% (95% CI 85.5–100; p<0.0001), demonstrating significant superiority over placebo.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints of radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival
brief_rationale: Both coprimary endpoints favored abiraterone in the overall population: radiographic progression-free survival HR 0.54 (99.9% CI 0.41-0.71; p<0.0001) and overall survival HR 0.82 (95.1% CI 0.69-0.98; p=0.030).

primary_endpoint_description: Number of monthly hereditary angioedema attacks during the 12-week subcutaneous administration period, comparing 200 mg and 600 mg garadacimab with placebo in the intention-to-treat population.
brief_rationale: Both prespecified primary comparisons favored garadacimab and were statistically significant: attack rates were reduced versus placebo by 100% with 200 mg (p=0.0002) and 93% with 600 mg (p=0.0003).

primary_endpoint_description: Vaccine efficacy against RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 of any severity from 14 days after dose 2 in baseline seronegative participants, together with safety and solicited local and systemic adverse events in the phase 2 subset.
brief_rationale: The efficacy primary endpoint favored SCB-2019 (67.2% efficacy; 95.72% CI 54.3–76.8), while safety/reactogenicity was also explicitly designated primary. The abstract does not state an overall success rule for these multiple primary endpoints or a formal success criterion for the safety endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Proportion of relatives with prolonged grief at 6 months after the patient's death, defined as a PG-13 score of 30 or higher.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies this as the primary endpoint and reports that the intervention significantly reduced prolonged grief symptoms versus standard care (p=0.035), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Metastasis-free survival
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival. Combination therapy significantly improved this endpoint versus ADT alone (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.44–0.64; p<0.0001), exceeding the stated one-sided significance criterion and favoring combination therapy.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary outcomes of safety and reactogenicity and immunogenicity measured by anti-spike IgG ELISA.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies safety/reactogenicity and anti-spike IgG immunogenicity as coprimary outcomes, but does not state an overall success rule or clear prespecified criteria integrating these outcomes. Although immunogenicity and safety findings are reported, overall primary-endpoint success cannot be determined.

primary_endpoint_description: Change in ESSDAI score from baseline to week 24, assessed for a dose-related response across ianalumab doses
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies change in ESSDAI at 24 weeks as the primary outcome and states that the study met its primary objective. Significant dose-response effects were observed in four of five prespecified models (p<0.025), demonstrating a favorable dose-related decrease in disease activity.

primary_endpoint_description: 28-day mortality
brief_rationale: The explicitly identified primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Mortality was 17% with aspirin and 17% with usual care (rate ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.89–1.04; p=0.35), so aspirin did not demonstrate favorable superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Percentage change in bodyweight from baseline to week 26, assessed using the trial product and treatment policy estimands.
brief_rationale: All cagrilintide doses produced greater mean percentage weight reductions than placebo for the primary endpoint under the trial product estimand (estimated treatment differences 3.0%–7.8%; p<0.001), with similar findings under the treatment policy estimand, meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: JIA flare rate by week 44 during part 2 among patients with polyarticular-course juvenile idiopathic arthritis
brief_rationale: The primary endpoint favored tofacitinib: flare occurred in 29% with tofacitinib versus 53% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.46, 95% CI 0.27–0.79; p=0.0031), demonstrating statistically significant superiority.

primary_endpoint_description: Non-inferiority of tirzepatide 10 mg or 15 mg, or both, versus insulin glargine for change in HbA1c from baseline to 52 weeks, using a 0.3% non-inferiority margin.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies this as the primary endpoint and reports that the prespecified 0.3% non-inferiority margin was met for both the 10 mg and 15 mg tirzepatide doses versus glargine.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary outcomes were COVID-19-related school absence and symptomatic PCR-confirmed COVID-19 adjusted for community case rates as an estimate of within-school transmission.
brief_rationale: The transmission coprimary outcome met the stated noninferiority margin: aIRR 0.96 (95% CI 0.75–1.22), with the upper bound below the allowed 1.50 relative increase. COVID-19-related absence was not significantly reduced (aIRR 0.80, 95% CI 0.54–1.19). Because the coprimary results are mixed and the abstract does not state the overall success rule or a success criterion for absence, overall primary-endpoint success is indeterminable.

primary_endpoint_description: Time to first stroke or systemic arterial embolism
brief_rationale: The primary outcome occurred in 4.5% of the ILR group versus 5.6% of the usual-care group (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.61–1.05; p=0.11), so ILR screening did not achieve a statistically significant favorable reduction.

The abstract reports procedural and non-procedural stroke outcomes but does not explicitly identify any endpoint as the prespecified primary endpoint; therefore primary-endpoint success cannot be assessed.

primary_endpoint_description: Non-inferiority of tirzepatide 10 mg or 15 mg, or both, versus insulin degludec for mean change from baseline in HbA1c at week 52, using a 0.3% non-inferiority margin.
brief_rationale: The abstract explicitly identifies this as the primary efficacy endpoint and reports that the prespecified 0.3% non-inferiority margin was met.

primary_endpoint_description: Mean change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) from baseline at 40 weeks
brief_rationale: All three tirzepatide doses produced significantly greater HbA1c reductions than placebo at 40 weeks, with estimated treatment differences of -1.91%, -1.93%, and -2.11% (all p<0.0001), meeting the favorable superiority criterion.

primary_endpoint_description: Primary efficacy outcome: hierarchical analysis of time to death, duration of hospitalization, or duration of supplemental oxygen through day 30 using the win ratio; primary safety outcome: major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding through 30 days.
brief_rationale: Therapeutic anticoagulation did not improve the primary efficacy outcome versus prophylactic anticoagulation (win ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.59–1.22; p=0.40) and significantly increased the primary safety bleeding outcome (8% vs 2%). The intended favorable superiority criterion was not met.

primary_endpoint_description: Clinical remission based on Mayo endoscopic, rectal bleeding, and stool frequency subscores at weeks 10 and 58.
brief_rationale: Filgotinib 200 mg produced significantly higher clinical remission rates than placebo at week 10 in both induction studies and at week 58 in maintenance, meeting the favorable superiority criterion for the explicitly identified primary endpoint.

primary_endpoint_description: Coprimary endpoints at week 16: the proportions of patients achieving EASI-75 and a vIGA-AD response (score 0 or 1 with at least 2 grades of improvement from baseline).
